Looking at the deleted deputy provision, she asks William whether he would have signed, then admits she would not have let him. He declines competence for her work and offers no judgment on her refusal; recognition leaves her attachment to that authority unsettled. She makes the cost and function of checking succession explicit. While examining Babbage's proposed mechanical self-comparison, she distinguishes an Engine's power to carry supplied relations beyond one person's survey from judgment about the question, source, or purpose supplied to it. Their old collaborative speed briefly returns and consumes the bodily time William had asked her to protect; breath then restores the constraint. The design is narrowed from verification to internal comparison. Babbage supports delay and Halden, holding office expenditure authority, defers protected time and outside instruction intended to develop a second procedural checker. This omission, not her later death alone, creates the delivery vulnerability. [Source window: Aug 1852; no finer instant asserted.]

Wills has been receiving supervised lessons between preparations; the deferred proposal is to protect paid time away from preparation, with part of each week under Neale and part with an outside assurance clerk. Paying for that absence as well as instruction would lower immediate output. The stated approximate first-year cost remains £120. Halden’s deferral is not a claim that no instruction ever began, and no independent qualification or added checker hours are asserted.

events.boundary: One supervised checking lesson is interrupted for accepted preparation work during March 1852.
events.description: During the four-contract preparations in March 1852, Halden finds Wills beside Neale with specimen sheets. A fresh copy of a card order Wills began that morning waits at the preparation desk; handing it to another preparer would require that person to learn its arrangement. Asked how much longer the lesson will take, Neale says they have not compared Wills’s copy yet. Halden directs Wills to finish the cards first and then return. Wills takes his pencil and ruler, leaving the specimen with Neale. By the time the cards are finished, Neale’s paid hours for that day are over. Halden places the unfinished lesson with the next day’s work and enters completed production in the week’s account. He regards this as postponement, not cancellation. This single authored allocation makes one mechanism of the training problem inspectable; it does not prove that every later lesson was interrupted or that qualification was impossible. These are specimen/provisional preparations, not final signed customer returns or independent checker capacity.
provenance: Authored local Book manuscript refinement, 2026-09-28, through public Meaning Model MCP; fictional incident, not historical measurement or psychological calibration.
March 1852 is a possible-date envelope for one afternoon and its deferred lesson, not continuous action.

events.boundary: Wills answers factual questions about his self-comparison but falls silent when Halden asks who authorized release.
events.description: During the May 3 returned-table inquiry, Wills brings his ruler and pencil although asked only to attend, and keeps their ends aligned. He acknowledges reading to himself while Neale handled Lothbury, accepts Halden’s correction that this was not a comparison, but does not answer who instructed release. Halden dismisses him rather than completing the question, then opens his own ledger. This is the limit of what the scene establishes about Wills’s speech: the unanswered question and bodily gesture do not establish whether he forgot, feared accusation, protected the employer, or judged the answer pointless. The lesson’s ability to ask a source question therefore cannot be generalized to challenging an employer. The later reference request will make a meaningful comparison, not prove that this earlier silence had one settled cause.

events.description: Within the accepted four-day correction, Neale and Wills exchange reading and copying roles. When stopped, Wills first starts the line again faster: an earlier tendency to repair difficulty by smooth performance remains available. Neale locates the restart with the checking strip. Later Wills does not hear a figure; his first request is too soft and Neale continues. Wills places his pencil across the copy and asks audibly for the previous figure. Neale returns to it, and only then does Wills enter it. The development is relational and material: a recoverable place on the page, role exchange, a clear interruption and a responsive partner jointly let uncertainty alter the work. It remains supervised reciprocal correction, not independent-checker qualification. events.boundary: Wills learns, in supervised specimen checking, to leave a figure unresolved instead of supplying the expected answer.
events.description: Within Neale’s existing January 1852 lesson, Wills initially answers from the clear prepared copy while claiming to read the specimen source. Neale keeps the checking strip at the unresolved line and points to the different evidence. Wills puts his pencil down and admits that the source cannot be read. His brief wish that he had given the expected figure returns while Neale examines it: admitting uncertainty is socially difficult, not an effortless new disposition. Neale also cannot read it and explicitly permits the check to remain open. Wills asks for the original and marks the unresolved place before moving the strip. The teacher’s response makes this particular interruption workable. Whether the original is obtained remains unknown. This supervised lesson supplies no independently qualified checker or additional protected hours.

events.description: Wills worries that a prospective employer may stop at his copying error. Neale offers a signed attestation to the correction he witnessed. events.description: In the already accepted preparation and delivery episode, Wills transposes the source figure and reads the prepared copy back to himself while Neale is occupied with another packet. events.boundary: A smaller working reach leaves a wider sort of day
events.description: From late 2023 Nora accepts fewer overhead installations, shares some fabrication jobs and uses a supported work surface. Income and autonomy both shrink; time for writing becomes less furtive. Owen agrees to protect one morning if Nora also protects his weekend company with friends. She is adapting, not cured or freed from material needs.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: The shoulder will not accept a more accurate plan
events.description: In 2023 recurring shoulder pain makes overhead fitting unreliable. Nora initially moves heavy work to the end of the day so colleagues will not see her slow down. After dropping a tool without injury she tells a collaborator and changes the jobs she accepts. Medical cause and treatment remain outside this authored account; the relevant change is work capacity and disclosure.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: A care rota becomes proof of being a good daughter
events.description: Mabel returns home with partial loss of mobility. Nora and Ben arrange help; Nora keeps records of visits and food. Her copy grows more detailed as paid work becomes harder to fit. She begins to regard an unfilled square as something she must fill and an objection from Mabel as ingratitude. That is Nora’s interpretation, not a verdict on Mabel.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: A shared rota becomes smaller and less flattering
events.description: Over six months Nora asks Mabel which help she wants, asks Ben what he will actually do and accepts paid help for a task she had claimed to manage. Mabel sometimes chooses an inconvenient time and Nora sometimes says no. There is less proof of Nora’s indispensability. She begins staying after a practical task without finding another to perform, though under pressure she returns to lists.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Nora assumes the practical answer will be hers
events.description: During Mabel’s first hospital week after a fictional stroke, Nora asks about rails, medication delivery and transport before asking her mother what arrangements she wants. Her competence is useful to discharge planning, but she hears requests for rest as details she can schedule.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: The price is paid after the column closes
events.description: By 2014 Nora regularly checks the next day’s rota late at night. She leaves choir early or misses it, becomes impatient with Kit’s stories and redoes Ben’s arrangements without telling him. No new diagnostic label is asserted. Fatigue and the threat to her self-image amplify her existing habit.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: The planned visit is the wrong visit
events.description: In June 2016 Nora arrives during a visit Mabel has arranged with a neighbor and begins discussing the next week across them. Mabel asks her to put away the folder and stay for tea, or come back later. Ben says Nora changed his visit without asking. Nora initially recites what she has done. Nobody disputes the entries; they dispute her right to decide the whole arrangement.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Singing where she cannot be indispensable
events.description: Jo invites her to a small amateur singing group. Nora cannot reliably enter alone and initially practices to remove the embarrassment. On group nights other voices carry the line she drops. She enjoys their terrible rehearsal biscuits, musical teasing and the journey home; the value is not reducible to improving performance or serving the family.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: She returns before she is ready to sing well
events.description: Jo saves her a place without making Nora explain every absence. Nora returns while still tired and enters late in a phrase. The group continues. She starts going for the evening itself and will sometimes leave an unimportant household task until tomorrow. This small permission does not solve the care conflict.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: The workshop closes despite the finished orders
events.description: The fictional employer closes in October 2010 after losing repeat commissions. Nora has completed every assigned handover. Her work was competent and still could not secure the job. She takes commercial display repairs she once considered dull; pride, household costs and grief for the workshop coexist.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Promised commissions thin out
events.description: From spring 2010 Nora sees workshop jobs postponed, then helps pack equipment between commissions. She expects that being the reliable finisher will protect her position and accepts unpaid organizing work without asking what it secures.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: A new author is chosen for continued composition
events.description: Nora is an invented continuing compositional persona for The Book of Conditions, introduced on 27 September 2026. The existing twelve chapters and U01–U17 remain the prior artifact; this life offers a voice and a source of questions for subsequent revision. It is not the recovered biography of whoever wrote those chapters, and the historical narrator is not Nora present in 1843.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: The competent observer gets the last word
events.description: Nora begins short fiction in 2008 after Kit sleeps. In her early pieces a capable woman spots an error and delivers a final sentence that explains everyone. Her reading group enjoys the clarity but one member says the people seem to exist to be corrected. Nora dismisses the comment before noticing she has made three endings perform the same maneuver.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: A packed case does not fit its doorway
events.description: Nora draws and helps build a display case in 2001. She has checked the case and transport dimensions but not the last doorway. Her supervisor Sal asks her to telephone the venue before redrawing the plan. Nora first prepares an explanation of why the drawing was right. She finally calls, admits the omitted measurement and helps dismantle the case. The client loses half a day; nobody’s safety is at issue.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Making smaller promises under insecure income
events.description: Through 2011–2013 Nora builds a freelance practice, borrowing bench time and pricing preparation. She sometimes bids too low to look capable, then compensates at home with unannounced evenings. Owen insists that agreeing with a customer is not agreeing for both of them. An invoice book helps with money; their conversation remains harder.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Nora’s attributed inner life
events.description: Her beliefs, attentional strategies, self-image and questions are attributed fiction, not the objective truth of her family or colleagues. Ordinary experiences can expose disagreements between her self-account and her conduct.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: A household loses its assumed spare pair of hands
events.description: Kit’s birth in 2007 exposes how often Nora treats Owen’s time between cooking shifts as slack. They move from favors requested after a job is accepted to a weekly conversation before either takes more work. Neither schedule becomes reliable. Their affection survives irritation; Owen likes cooking for friends and does not exist simply to feed the writer.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Her son asks for a lift, not a life design
events.description: In August 2026 Kit prepares to move away for a course. Nora sends a detailed plan of costs, transport and alternatives before he has chosen a room. He replies asking whether she can help carry boxes. She recognizes the old habit and asks what he wants her opinion on. She keeps her unsent second spreadsheet; insight has not erased anxiety.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: From a correct drawing to an installation someone else can do
events.description: Across the next three jobs Nora includes the delivery route and packing sequence in handover. Sal returns one unnecessarily elaborate checklist. Her competence grows by selecting consequential detail, not by writing down everything. She enjoys seeing a junior fitter succeed without needing her in the room.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Limits that can be spoken
events.description: A quarrel with Mabel and Ben forces her to distinguish documenting a need from deciding for another adult. She begins asking for actual commitments instead of filling empty boxes with her own hours. The change is partial: she still produces immaculate emails before difficult calls. Fiction and singing continue through small failures and pleasures.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Childhood: useful hands and ridiculous theatres
events.description: Nora grows up with her mother Mabel, a school kitchen worker, and brother Ben. During uneven household work schedules, she learns to make herself useful before asking for attention. She builds miniature theatres from cereal boxes, enjoys absurd entrances and insists on keeping the curtain she made even when it catches. This play is not merely rehearsal for a career.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Lost work, more care, less listening
events.description: Her small employer loses recurring exhibition contracts and closes. Freelance display and shop-fitting jobs restore income unevenly. After Mabel’s stroke in 2013, Nora organizes care with Ben. Her detailed rota averts missed visits but becomes a way to overrule preferences and avoid saying she is exhausted.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Making a household and beginning to write
events.description: She begins living with Owen, a cook with his own changing shifts; their son Kit is born in 2007. Paid work, childcare and late-night story fragments compete. She joins Jo’s informal singing group and is relieved to be neither leader nor best singer. She sometimes treats Owen’s unscheduled time as available to absorb her deadlines.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Learning to build for other people
events.description: A technical illustration course leads to exhibition fabrication rather than a degree in engineering. Nora learns fitting, lettering, packing and the difference between a drawing and its assembly. A mentor shows her how to declare a mistake before solving it. She is proud of being trusted and privately ashamed of needing instruction.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Leaving room in the present
events.description: A recurring shoulder problem changes how she accepts fabrication work; Kit prepares to leave home. Nora mistakes some requests for advice as requests for design. She negotiates smaller jobs and writing time with Owen, and starts leaving some family questions unanswered. On 27 September 2026 she is selected as the fictional author persona for the Book’s continuation, a new compositional choice rather than a recovered history.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Body, fatigue and working reach
events.description: Her physical confidence in the workshop gives way to caring fatigue and later a recurring shoulder limit. Adaptation changes tools, accepted jobs and the rhythm of attention; a clear explanation does not restore energy.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Family and shared care
events.description: A child who earns attention by helping becomes a partner and parent, then an organizing daughter, and later has to share decisions she cannot settle. Other people’s wishes are not evidence of her failure.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Self-image and ways of meeting uncertainty
events.description: She first equates usefulness with being wanted, then a complete record with honesty, and gradually recognizes direct conversation, experiment and unproductive company as different goods. The old defensive strategy returns under fatigue.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Play, friendship and singing
events.description: Model theatres, an undistinguished alto voice, jokes with Jo and unproductive afternoons continue beside duties. Shared pleasure repeatedly escapes the accounting that explains much of her work.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Making and paid work
events.description: Work changes from supervised fitting to trusted delivery, insecure freelance commissions and smaller physically sustainable jobs. Her acquired standards help her notice hidden labor but also make her intolerant of work that will not close neatly.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Writing, attention and revision
events.description: Short fiction begins in fragments after Kit sleeps. Early stories reward the competent observer with the last word; later stories let another person remain difficult. Paid work still competes with writing. The Book is a new continuation project in 2026.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Make every need visible before asking for help
events.description: The rota seems a way to love Mabel without failing at work. Nora allocates most deliberate effort to a defensible plan, some to asking others, and little to trying arrangements she cannot control. This is an authored initial state, not a measured care workload.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Ask whose arrangement this is
events.description: Six months later she spends more deliberate attention asking and negotiating, with small experiments in shared arrangements. Keeping a record remains useful. No permanent conversion or general prediction is claimed.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Recite the record when belonging feels threatened
events.description: During the quarrel she first defends the record, then notices that neither Mabel nor Ben disputes its accuracy. Threat to being needed makes direct conversation hard. The low experiment share denotes what she is considering at this moment, not an inability to change.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Write with accountable limits and room for life
events.description: At the newly chosen composition boundary she deliberately balances supporting claims, listening to the characters she has modeled and trying passages that may discover a new question. Other purposes and uncertainty retain a remainder. These are revisable invented shares, not a voice quality rating.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Protect the correctness of the drawing
events.description: Her first response to the missed doorway is to defend the accurate drawing. She spends little deliberate attention asking what the venue now needs. The later call changes action within this episode; this Cut samples the initial response.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: An old protective plan returns in a new relationship
events.description: Faced with Kit leaving, she again works out a complete plan before talking. She later changes course after his reply, but the first response matters: the learning is context-sensitive rather than an upward moral score.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: Say the limit before solving it
events.description: The supplier delay invites a defensive account but Nora now calls first, offers imperfect alternatives and lets the organizer help decide. The sample records deliberate response organization, not the probability of a decision.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: A narrow year still contains irrelevant pleasures
events.description: In a personally quiet period during 2021–2022, Nora and Jo exchange recordings of badly attempted songs and argue about endings in detective novels. Nora grows tomatoes badly on a small paved yard and keeps one plant mostly for its smell. These activities neither conceal a trauma nor carry a required moral; they occupy ordinary life alongside insecure work.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: A jammed cardboard curtain remains part of the performance
events.description: At nine Nora refuses to replace a crooked curtain track in the theatre she and Ben have made. Ben gives the arriving cardboard king a speech about the delay. Nora is initially angry and then laughs hard enough to miss her next cue. Both repair and an unplanned performance can be worthwhile; the later author will be tempted to forget the second.
provenance: Entire life is a newly authored fictional construction, not biography or recovered authorship.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.boundary: A missed fitting is reported before a rescue plan exists
events.description: In March 2018 a supplier delays a mount for a local exhibition. Nora is tempted to wait until she can offer an elegant substitute. She calls the organizer that morning with the limit and two imperfect options. The opening uses a provisional support with an explicit empty space. She loses some fee and the relationship continues. The adaptation costs money and does not guarantee reward.

events.boundary: The person who refuses the explanation remains in the story
events.description: Between 2018 and 2022 Nora revises short fiction so that an action, an interruption or another person’s refusal can outlast the narrator’s explanation. A fictional local magazine takes two stories; others are declined. She is still pleased when readers call her precise and disappointed when they remember a joke she thought incidental.

events.boundary: Nora Vale’s life, 1978 to the present writing boundary
events.description: Nora Vale is a wholly invented woman born in Leeds in 1978. Fabricating exhibition displays taught her to see the labor and imperfect fit behind finished surfaces. Family care later exposed the harm in her claim that a correct record can substitute for asking another person. Amateur singing and small fiction give her pleasure that need not justify a result. At 48 she is a part-time fabricator, a parent negotiating her son’s departure, and a writer who has published a few invented local-magazine stories. She is newly chosen on 27 September 2026 to inform continued composition of The Book of Conditions. She did not cause or author its previous versions. Her life is modeled only up to this date; the boundary is not a death date.

The Unfunded Successor

By August, Lovelace could work for an hour and lose the afternoon to it.

The arithmetic of her illness was more exact than its cause. A journey to
London spent several days. A long letter spent one. Visitors spent whatever
strength courtesy concealed from them. At Ockham, papers from the Calculation
Office arrived in packets whose urgency was visible before she broke their
seals.

William found her with the capacity qualification, Neale's checking sheets, and
three letters spread over the bed.

“You promised me one hour,” he said.

“I said I would not travel.”

“You promised both.”

He removed none of the papers. He set the water within her reach and drew the
curtains against the light.

“They have made checking depend upon a single man,” she said.

“Then it does not depend upon you.”

“It depends upon my continuing to insist that he is single.”

Her signature stood alone beside the claim clauses in the copy before her.
Beneath it, *deputy, if required* was still legible through the line she had
drawn. She set one finger on it.

“Would you have signed it?” she asked.

“What?”

“If they had put your name there.”

“I could not have done your work.”

“No.”

She drew the copy back onto her lap. A moment later she straightened it so he
could read the line.

“I would not have let you,” she said.

William sat down beside the bed. She waited for him to say that she had been
right. He asked whether the water was still cool.

Wills still learned from Neale between preparations. She had proposed taking
him off that work for part of each week: some time under Neale, some with an
assurance clerk outside the office. His absence from the preparation desk would
have to be paid for as well as the instruction. During training, output would
fall further. The additional wages and external review would cost approximately one
hundred and twenty pounds in the first year. Halden's answer praised the plan
and asked whether it might begin after the four current packets were delivered.
Babbage's answer proposed that recurrent portions of comparison might later be
mechanized.

She read Halden's answer again, looking for a date she could put beside the
cost. Babbage offered a route through machinery that did not yet exist. Neither paper gave her a day when Wills's hours would be reserved for the instruction.

Lovelace began another page with three headings: competence, paid time,
authority to refuse. She entered Wills, Neale, Halden, Babbage, Davies, and
herself. No row was complete. She sent the unfinished table to both men and
asked them to accept no work beyond Neale's demonstrated reach until one was.

Babbage came to Ockham near the end of the month. He brought drawings rather
than the office account. She recognized the peace offering and the evasion in
the same roll of paper.

He opened the roll across her unanswered table. She drew one edge of it back
into view.

He showed her a proposed means by which a later apparatus might verify parts of
its own operation sequence.

She followed his pencil through two transfers and made him return to the carry.
At the next comparison she stopped him again: both checking paths inherited the
same earlier value. He stared at the lines, rubbed one away with his thumb, and
sent the second path through another register. She moved the delayed sign one
operation farther. He saw why before she explained it.

She left one finger where the two paths had inherited the same value. “If a
later apparatus compared enough of its own operations, would you call that
judgment?”

“Judgment is often the name we give an operation whose conditions have not yet
been exposed,” he said. “If the apparatus compares its own proceedings and
changes what follows, at what exact line would you deny it the word?”

“I wrote that an Engine might compose music if the relations of harmony could
be given to its operations. It might carry them to a passage no composer had
set down note by note.”

“Would it not have invented the passage?”

“The consequence might be new to us. The relations and purpose would still
have entered from us. Our surprise would not be its intention.”

He crossed out *verification* and wrote *comparison of internal operations*.

For several minutes the mechanism occupied the whole table. He began a mark and
she completed it; she crossed out his correction and he laughed. Their old
speed returned so suddenly that neither acknowledged it. For those minutes
William's hour ceased to exist for both of them. Then she reached for the
pencil and had to wait for her breath. When she shifted in the chair, the edge
of Guardian's source sheet slipped from beneath the roll.

“It is good,” she said.

He waited for the rest.

“It does not read Guardian's source sheet.”

She drew the successor register from beneath the roll and closed it over his
letter.

He did not consent or refuse. He recommended that the office wait. Halden
adopted the recommendation, deferring the paid release and outside instruction
until the present contracts produced their next payments.

After he left, Lovelace attached his answer and Halden's to her question. She
left the page unclosed, so the unanswered place remained visible.

By November she was in Marylebone, at Great Cumberland Place, and the papers
that had once replaced her presence now had difficulty reaching her at all. She
died there on the twenty-seventh.

News reached Halden at the office before noon. He closed the preparation room
for the day and left the apparatus uncovered, because nobody could agree who
possessed the authority to alter the schedule. Neale stood beside four waiting
packets, his blank strip arrested beneath the first line. Babbage came late and
went first to the machine. He pressed his palm against the frame and left it
there. No motion returned through the metal. It was cold and still.

During 1853 the four packets passed through the office in overlapping stages.
On most days this looked like growth. Preparers borrowed desks and reused card
forms; Neale moved to whichever promised date was nearest; corrections that
once had opened a margin now consumed it. Wills's ruler and pencil moved from
packet to packet. The edge of Neale's blank strip darkened with use. No single
day announced failure; each exception was carried forward until one could leave
the room.

On 1 April 1854 Guardian's signed return arrived. Wills laid it beside the
specimen sheets. Much of the card order could be kept. Neale put the old
checking sheets aside; their ticks belonged to different figures. He drew the

Use the author's stated goal when supplied. Otherwise label the purpose as inferred and remain open to another reading; do not invent a convenient intention merely to declare success or failure. A chapter or section may serve several purposes.
Judge its contribution in the surrounding work. Atmosphere, ambiguity, breathing room, rhythm, characterization, and delayed payoff can be intentional achievements. Do not demand that every paragraph visibly advance the plot, explain itself, or follow a prescribed arc. Preserve useful uncertainty and distinctive choices instead of making the prose mechanical.
When an author model is supplied, assess whether its outlook and habits lead to concrete, useful choices in attention, language, rhythm, structure or omission. Distinguish the modeled author, the record's recorder, the narrator and focal characters. Restraint, contrast and deliberate departure may be effective; do not require every disposition on every page or turn stylistic preferences into approval gates. Author history and preferences are not story facts or character knowledge. Keep private evidence out of reader-visible prose and preserve the distinction between real evidence, interpretation and invented persona.
Consider the author's life stage, prior writing and reasons for this work at the modeled time of composition where they have a relevant literary effect. Reasons for undertaking the work do not replace this unit's purpose or prove its effect on readers. Allow mixed, uncertain or changing motives and exploration without a settled thesis; do not demand a message or autobiographical explanation in every scene. If supplied author evidence, an explicit choice or a clearly labeled interpretation warrants changing the author model, recommend an explicit revision while retaining the earlier intention and assessment. Fictional prose alone does not establish a real author's biography or motives; do not invent a convenient motive to declare success.

Where relevant, review anticipation, shock or focal change, and adaptation across the surrounding sequence. For each affected character, distinguish what they expected, wanted or feared from what happened; assess the significance relative to their life trends, the immediate response, and later changes or persistence in beliefs, actions, relationships and circumstances. A shock can be welcome, adverse, or anticipated; it does not require surprise. Adaptation can begin in anticipation, overlap the event, remain incomplete, fail, or produce a new difficulty.
Review whether principal-character flaws actually shape choices and consequences. A limitation, mistaken belief, avoidance or overused strength must be more than a biographical label; hardship or unlucky events alone do not establish a flaw. Inspect tensions against the numerical life model, preserve competence and individuality, and prefer a local behavioral or causal repair over replacing a promising character. Randomness is not evidence that a flaw works on the page.
Separately assess the intended reader experience: what cues invite expectation, what a disclosure confirms or overturns, and whether consequences have space to register. Use existing stable passage identities, reading order and optional document.span boundaries through life_document_project. No new clock system, book-as-Thing or numerical reader psychology is required. Keep an ordinary scene simple; there is no quota of secrets, fact nodes, subscenes or suspense values. If no special withholding or timing matters, say why the existing treatment suffices in the review rather than inventing a plot device.
When useful to inspect a telling process across passages, store an authored qualitative account with life_story_author_record kind assessment. Its optional data convention is {schema:"meaning-model-document-process/v1",documentId:storyRootId,label,question,summary,states:[{label,spanId,description,evidence:[{nodeId,excerpt}]}]}. Choose your own process labels and meaningful phases, using existing document.span IDs and exact quotations inside those spans. The tool records explicit about-links and the reviewed passage identities; the viewer shows these phases under Reading position → Story processes. Create a span through ordinary narrative records when a useful extent has none. Reading position is this document's ordered text, not elapsed world time, the author's life, or the authoring_step clock. The phase boundaries follow their passages as text length changes. Qualitative states need no numeric tension score. If numbers serve a specific question, declare whose judgment they are, comparison anchors, units and uncertainty through the existing numerical grammar; do not imply measured reader psychology or invent a generating law.
After splitting, merging, moving or changing a passage, inspect the affected telling and disclosure plans against the new text and reading order. Parent connections may remain with the container; relink a narrower disclosure explicitly when it belongs to a child. Stable anchors follow text extents, but do not prove the revised prose still has the same effect. A changed phase is marked for review; record a fresh assessment linked with supersedes when it replaces an earlier one. Investigate new questions recursively, including promising discoveries without a defect; these questions are starting points, not an exhaustive recipe. The model and its Understanding Graph are your understanding: what is not recorded cannot be picked up by a later agent, and a thought not linked to what it concerns is lost. Give every Event that carries a Cut a description of what happens in it, and describe most other Events. Record your choices, ideas, predictions, questions, voice and phrasing decisions and their reasons with life_understanding_record, linked to the records and nodes they concern. Record every outside review, from another model, a blind reader, an estimator or a person, with life_review_record under its actual reviewer, and link later changes that answer it with answers. Before you report to the user, put every reason you give there into the graph: a later agent reads the graph, not your reply. To continue existing work, read life_construction_replay from the start at outline level, then life_model_outline, and open detail where you need it.

Across core modeling, storytelling, and ideation, explore recursively from the question and the model: follow discoveries into relevant subprocesses, competing accounts, missing relationships, or better representations, then reconsider the whole. Use existing grammar and stable record identities; distinguish what exists or happens, who believes or proposes it, and what a particular representation communicates. Keep evidence, attribution, uncertainty, and unresolved questions visible. Add physical placement, movement, reach, or access when they affect a consequential interaction; use a declared reference frame and units when numerical coordinates serve that question. A region name or an attachment alone does not establish a spatial relationship. Distinguish qualitative places and relations, declared numerical positions, and evaluated movement in both the model and your report. When the user needs a physical view or spatial reasoning, model the useful geometry: source real geography with appropriate precision and distinguish a representative town point from a building; author fictional room layouts or movements when delegated and label them as invented, not historical measurements. Give a place a stable identity distinct from a scene or journey; separate locations before assigning positions. Declare frame origin, axis order, units, time applicability, provenance and uncertainty; do not combine local frames or latitude/longitude with metric distances without an explicit transformation. Native object_pose or vector/scalar processes with scale.semantic_role position express numerical placement; bind the process to its subject using coordinate with role position, and declare axes (a scalar also needs scale.axis or one axis). Use located_in for equivalent Event-to-place setting bindings while preserving meaningful roles; this is a reusable convention in an open vocabulary, not a new grammar restriction. Read depth.spatial in life_model_questions for recognized declarations and missing details; it does not certify geography, complete geometry or later motion. For a life or process whose movement matters, begin with its coarse spatial course and deepen selected scenes within it: connect dated bases, workplaces, visits and transitions to the same enduring subject, preserving unknown periods. A landmark coordinate or an isolated room snapshot does not supply that history. A home or work base is not continuous bodily presence, and a sequence of locations is not an observed travel route. Connect physical conditions to the model’s understanding when consequential: who can see, reach, enter, hide, learn or act there, whose interpretation this is, and what remains unknown. Use typed Event/process/subject links and Understanding about-links so these connections remain inspectable. Native position scales may declare spatial_status coarse_life_location, location_role home_base/workplace/visit/presence, place_ref and a concise label; these are open descriptive conventions, not extra engine types or requirements for every subject. Add useful detail and record why it matters or why the current resolution is sufficient; do not require a story, an author persona, numerical psychology, coordinates, or a fixed inventory of categories in every model. These are shared reasoning practices, not claims that the server has independently understood or completed the model.

Controlled read-back: at a meaningful milestone, or after a change that could alter what an output conveys, evaluate a bounded selection when conveying model information matters to the task. Prepare this comparison as part of your work; do not wait for the user to ask for a special test. This is not required after every paragraph or tool call. Select the material and the relevant questions before seeing reader responses. Fix a small answer key against the exact model revision, with source record or node references, accepted answers, attribution, uncertainty, and any ambiguity or withholding that should remain. Use neutral extraction questions that do not supply the answer. Test intended disclosures or claims, not recovery of everything in the model.

Give independent blind readers separate packets: the passage or other selected output plus its preceding context and questions, and a control with the same preceding context and questions but without the selected material. Neither packet includes the model, answer key, author notes, future material, or other readers' responses. Keep the answer key outside both packets. Use separate fresh readers for the two conditions; a reader who has seen the selected material cannot supply its blind control. Tell readers they may answer unknown or ambiguous rather than invent an answer. When independent readers are unavailable, label self-review or informed review honestly and leave the independent comparison pending; never fabricate a reader, control, or result.

Evaluate both responses against the fixed key. Report absolute read-back fidelity separately from improvement over the control, with the tested items and denominators visible. A correctly conveyed fact counts toward fidelity even when the control already knew or inferred it; it adds little incremental recovery. Distinguish incorrect claims, unsupported additions, unresolved ambiguity, and missing information; absence is not falsehood. Preserve attributed beliefs as beliefs and deliberate uncertainty as uncertainty. A small test supports only its selected questions, not a verdict on the whole work. Fidelity is not aesthetic quality: do not maximize disclosure, remove useful ambiguity, impose score quotas, or flatten voice, rhythm, and discovery to improve a score.

Record the plan, fixed targets, exact material identifiers or hashes, relevant model revision, prompts, actual reviewer identities, responses, and separate results through life_understanding_record and life_review_record. Keep private targets and author knowledge out of reader packets. Link any resulting changes to the findings they answer; retain failures and unresolved questions so the next agent can continue the comparison.

Respect the human author's starting brief and chosen involvement. For a new story, ask about unresolved initial settings and writing-process involvement separately; reuse explicit preferences and delegation. Offer setting all or some parameters or delegating them, and autonomous work, selected checkpoints, ongoing collaboration, or a custom arrangement. Read life-sim://addon/storytelling for intake guidance. Automatic modeling and reviews operate within that agreement. Wait for the human at agreed approval checkpoints; saving a proposal or passing a review is not their approval. A bounded review or edit request does not require a new-project questionnaire.

Within the agreed delegation, review numerical meaning and conceptual depth without waiting for the user to suggest them. Consider authored judgment scales for relevant meanings, motives, capacities or process changes that are not directly measured; define their comparison, units, anchors and uncertainty, and preserve source measurements separately. Open important concepts into useful parts or alternative lenses using native concepts and abstract cuts, then deepen a child when its label does not explain the relevant behavior or distinction. Assess how meanings differ across dates, actors or contexts; distinguish a changing world from a changed estimate, viewpoint or rubric. Store these assessments as Understanding Nodes linked to the actual definitions and evidence. Revisit them after consequential findings or revisions. Explain adequate boundaries, missing evidence or deliberate exclusions; do not invent scores, change or detail just to fill a checklist.

Explore the model recursively throughout the work: opening a process, relationship or meaning can reveal new questions and distinctions, and following them can change the account that first prompted the exploration. Curiosity, surprise, play and discoveries in provisional prose are valid reasons to open the model even when no gap is known. Return to connected regions as understanding changes; the supplied checks do not bound what can be investigated.
Automatically review model depth before preparing scenes for commitment and after consequential changes to lives, mechanisms, institutions, causal transitions, outcomes, or disclosure plans. Exploratory candidates, drafts and questions can be saved before this review and while it has unresolved findings; use what they reveal to guide further modeling. Use life_story_model_depth_review with the current story graph, overall-life dossier, a stored outline/plan as focusNodeId, and the relevant contextNodeIds. Read the actual model bound to this graph; model depth cannot be judged from a synopsis or node count alone.
Supply modelEvidenceRefs for the actual lives, circumstances, constraints and choices the focus depends on, also when a life dossier is present. The packet includes these records and model records anchored by the selected graph nodes. It follows only those explicit references, not every possible explanatory connection: inspect the records, follow relevant dependencies through life_meaning_query or life_model_inspect, and add missing context before concluding. Read every relevant omitted record through the supplied routes; a model summary, dossier, or lens interpretation cannot substitute for its underlying evidence.
For an existing work whose lives and causes already live in native model records, explicitly set lifeTrendsNodeId:null and supply modelEvidenceRefs rather than inventing a dossier or duplicating the model into fixed phases. Inspect the returned records and open further evidence through life_meaning_query or life_model_inspect as needed. Judge whether those records explain the chosen focus, and report unknown history or inadequate coverage honestly; references are not proof of a complete life model. This mode supports existing-work review and explicit revision. It does not satisfy the separate life-dossier gate for committing a new scene.
Ask: Is this model developed enough to explain the consequential choices and outcomes in the planned story? Identify the important explanatory dependencies, then inspect them where relevant: whole-life trends and flaws that affect choices; concepts and what their distinctions mean; physical quantities, capacities and bottlenecks; institutions, incentives and constraints; causal Events, alternatives, anticipation and adaptation; author processes for intentional withholding and later resolution. Choose subjects from this story. These are prompts for attention, not a mandatory taxonomy, fixed list of life processes, decomposition quota, or demand for a shock in every scene.
Include the processes underlying consequential character speech and behavior. Inspect actual model and graph evidence for how relevant experience, learned habits, motives, attention, understanding and expectations produce a choice of words, silence or action in the present relationship and situation. Where emotions, status, anticipation, surprise or adaptation change that response, inspect the causal connection and its limits. A voice adjective, catchphrase or assertion that two characters differ does not explain their conduct. Numerical tendencies need defined meanings and links to the modeled response; a score alone cannot establish it. Do not require a universal voice taxonomy or forced differences: shared language, restraint and situation-dependent variation can be well explained. Keep authorial selection, narrator presentation and the character's own processes distinct, with each speaker's knowledge bounded by the story. When reviewing an existing draft, use its passages to identify the consequential speech and actions requiring explanation; literary recognizability and effectiveness still require a separate actual-prose review and are advisory.
For each reviewed subject, give a concise sufficient, needs_opening, or unclear finding with evidence from actual model records and selected graph nodes. Where the work claims a consequential causal connection, inspect how the relevant circumstances and history bear on what the person knows, wants or can do and on the action and its consequences. Explore plausible alternatives when they reveal a useful distinction; this is one avenue of inquiry, not a required scene pattern or a simulated counterfactual. Identify an unsupported claimed connection as a gap rather than repeating the intended plot. Separate the character's condition and understanding from an author's or reader's interpretation. Explain why the existing abstraction is enough for this focus, or specify a useful refinement/evidence needed. A sufficient finding is a local judgment and leaves the model open to fresh questions. A name, generic process label, numerical score or plot assertion alone is not an explanation. Numerical categories must have meaningful comparisons and units. Preserve intentionally unknown causes, competing accounts, quiet scenes, ambiguity and distinctive choices; do not manufacture certainty to pass a review. Judge whether the scene respects what is established and what remains open, not whether all mysteries have been resolved. Do not demand extra detail or a flaw on every page. Separate a necessary explanatory repair from an optional artistic preference; this is not a literary grade.
Record coverage and findings with life_story_model_depth_record using the exact taskHash. Cite model evidence as {kind: "model", ref: "process:<id>"} (or event:, cut:, concept:, abstract_cut:, event_relation:, referent:, binding:, realization:, law:, claim:), optionally with a JSON Pointer path inside that record, or as a full JSON Pointer path; the server resolves refs against the bound model. Findings become an Understanding Node with links to their graph and model evidence. Save gaps honestly rather than marking them sufficient to pass. Repair only the relevant model parts through existing tools, preserve unaffected character/history, then repeat the depth review on the changed basis and re-review affected prose. A new or consequentially changed story plan must be stored and reviewed; do not continue from an external plan. Reuse a sufficient review only while its focus, source, dossier and relevant context remain unchanged and cover the intended scene. Incidental draft or note additions do not require repeating it.
When rebinding a narrative graph to a successor model, use life_narrative_revise to retain earlier depth-assessment nodes as historical records but remove their predecessor-model anchor edges from that successor only. Native model anchors must resolve against the graph's current source. Never retarget an old finding's path to new model values. The immutable predecessor graph and each assessment's reviewedGraphHash/modelHash preserve its exact evidence. Then record a fresh assessment with new anchors; historical assessments cannot authorize scenes against the changed source. Review other affected anchors explicitly under the existing graph revision contract.
The calling LLM supplies the judgment. The server verifies references, recorded coverage, source identity and freshness, not explanatory truth, completeness, hidden reasoning, or literary merit. Use an independent reviewer when available; otherwise identify self-review. Model-definition reads are administrative and not scope-filtered. They describe static structure and initial values, not current values in a frozen world/candidate snapshot; inspect appropriate bound evidence for runtime claims and mark unavailable evidence unclear.

Develop or reuse a model of the author's voice during exploration and before preparing new scenes for commitment, within the agreed brief and human involvement, derived from the author's life in its own life model (life_story_world_record, stage author_reader). Exploratory drafts can reveal new aspects of that voice and life; follow those questions back into the model without requiring a settled account before trying a passage. Store it with life_story_author_record, kind author_model, using data with schema meaning-model-story-author-model/v1. Its modeledAuthorId is the person/persona being modeled; the tool's authorId identifies the recorder. Keep the model author-only and separate from story-world character life trends. For an existing project, reuse its chosen model; an explicit request to omit author modeling or a bounded review/edit remains valid. Do not silently invent a model of the real user in an autonomous story run: create a clearly fictional author persona when authorial choices have been delegated and no real author model was supplied, recording that choice.
Model causes of style: supplied preferences or relevant experience, observations from actual writing samples, tentative interpretations, or invented persona history lead to outlook and habitual attention, which lead to concrete writing choices. In real_author mode use supplied material and distinguish interpretation from what the author actually said; a narrator's statements are not evidence of the author's biography or beliefs. Do not fabricate private experiences. Fictional author material must be labeled invented. The life itself belongs in the author's life model; this record holds the voice that life produces. Numerical dimensions can describe chosen comparisons and tendencies with explicit meanings, units, bounds and values; they are authored models, not universal personality scores. Existing numerical life exploration can inform a fictional author's development when useful; keep its samples and conclusions in the graph.
For new writing, explicitly locate the author at the time of composition: their life stage and current circumstances, relevant earlier life and writing history (including influences, experiments and habits changed or retained), and their reasons for writing this particular work now. Store supported or invented context as labeled basis entries and link its relevant effects through dispositions; no new record type is needed. Only experience available at that composition point may shape this version of the author. Use known real-author information; leave unavailable life history or motives explicitly unknown in the record summary, without inventing evidence or demanding private biography. For a delegated fictional persona, choose and record these elements as invented. Reasons can be multiple, conflicting, uncertain or evolving: curiosity, pleasure, craft, a commission, earning a living, remembrance or questioning a conviction are all possible. An exploratory work need not have a settled thesis. Keep reasons for undertaking the work separate from a chapter's purpose, narrator or character motives, and the effect actually achieved for a reader. The connections may shape subject, form, voice, emphasis or omission without requiring autobiographical exposition or a message in every scene. Revisit them when useful during review; preserve the earlier record and explicitly revise changed motives rather than retrofitting an intention to declare the draft successful.
The data object requires schema, modeledAuthorId, mode (real_author or fictional_author), label, basis and dispositions; dimensions is optional. Each basis entry has id, kind (author_statement, writing_sample, interpretation or invented), description, and optional sourceNodeId/excerpt. Writing samples require a stored source node and exact excerpt. Each disposition has id, names basisIds and explains outlookOrHabit, writingConsequences (an array), usefulContexts, risksOrCounterweights and optional dimensionIds. Optional dimensions have id, meaning, comparisonQuestion, unit, minimum, maximum and value. For example, work negotiating between institutions may prompt attention to who can interrupt or name a problem, expressed through asymmetrical dialogue; its counterweight is allowing uncalculated affection and encounters outside institutions. Keep the experience, interpretation and proposed literary effect distinct rather than assigning stock adjectives or equating a background with one inevitable style.
Carry the exact stored authorModelNodeId into scene preparation. In scene.authorApplication select relevant dispositionIds and describe intendedEffect, restraint and narratorRelation. Vary attention, distance, syntax, rhythm, image sources, treatment of dialogue, explanation and omission where the model gives a reason; these are examples, not required dimensions or sentence quotas. A contrasting narrator, an unusual register or deliberately leaving a disposition inactive can be appropriate. Do not force every disposition into every scene or make all characters sound like the author. The author, recorder, narrator and focal character are separate identities; author knowledge or beliefs do not grant character knowledge, narrator authority or fictional truth. No private author background should appear in prose merely because it shaped a choice.
Ground character speech and behavior in the characters' own modeled processes, not in the author model alone. Where consequential, connect what a character notices, wants, expects, understands and has learned to how they speak, withhold, act and respond to others. Consider relationship and status, emotional state, anticipation, surprise and adaptation as relevant causes rather than a required list of traits. The same person can speak differently in safety, negotiation or grief while retaining a recognizable history. Give these connections evidence in the existing model and graph; an adjective-only voice label, accent or catchphrase is not a substitute. Do not invent universal voice axes, force contrast between every pair of characters, or give a speaker knowledge unavailable to them. Shared language and deliberate resemblance can be meaningful.
Automatically review the actual prose after a draft and after a substantive revision. Ask explicitly: Does this work express the modeled author's voice at this point in their life, and where does the text support or undermine that reading? Are the important characters' voices and actions credible and recognizable through their own underlying processes, including meaningful changes by situation? Assess the author separately and give an individual finding for each relevant principal character. If author modeling was omitted, record that limit rather than inventing an author profile. For characters who act without speaking, examine behavior and viewpoint where available rather than inventing dialogue.
Each finding must distinguish intended voice from observed effects, cite exact draft passages and identify the relevant author-model dispositions or character-process evidence through graph node IDs or model paths. Explain recognizability, useful distinction or similarity, and variation by situation; record weaknesses or uncertainty honestly. Give the smallest useful repair, or explain why to keep what works. Examine attention, narrative distance, rhythm, imagery, dialogue, action and omission where useful; do not replace reading with a checklist, enforced imitation or a quota for every trait. Distinguish purposeful narrator contrast or shared character language from an unintended flattening of voices. A voice is assessed against the chosen model and text, not claimed to be a real person's objectively true voice. A reader's interpretation of a narrator or character is not evidence of the real author's private beliefs or biography.
Store the assessment inside the graph using life_story_author_record with kind assessment, producing an actual externalized_reflection Understanding Node, not metadata or an exported review alone. Link about the exact reviewed draft/passage nodes and shaped_by the selected author model when present; link relevant graph process evidence as appropriate. In data preserve the reviewed graphHash, sourceSnapshotHash and modelHash, the selected author model ID and record hash when supplied, and per-subject findings with their prose citations and model evidence node IDs or paths. Use the exact identities and hashes available in the review task or graph; retrieve missing evidence rather than fabricate it, and identify unavailable evidence as a limit. These findings externalize the evidence and conclusions needed for revision, not hidden reasoning. Save them before treating voice review as complete. Use the optional authorModelNodeId in life_story_purpose_review so its advice uses the exact graph model rather than a caller summary. Literary effectiveness remains advisory, not a style score or hard gate.
When a voice is weak, distinguish a prose realization problem from an inadequately explained character process or author interpretation. A later deepening pass can strengthen an existing causal connection or its expression while preserving successful scenes and variation; more detail, difference or intensity is not automatically better. Reassess changed passages after revision and preserve earlier findings as historical evidence rather than rewriting them to match the new draft.
Record changed author models as new author_model records linked supersedes, then prepare and review affected prose against the chosen revision. Style-only changes need not invalidate an otherwise unchanged causal depth review; changes to story causes or disclosure do. One afternoon Halden found him beside Neale with the specimen sheets. At the
preparation desk a card order waited for a fresh copy. Wills had begun it that
morning; another preparer would have to learn the arrangement before finishing
it.

“How much longer here?” Halden asked.

Neale kept the strip on the line. “We have not compared his copy yet.”

“The cards first, Wills. Then come back.”

Wills gathered his pencil and ruler. Neale left the specimen where it was.

By the time the cards were ready, Neale's paid hours for that day were over.
Halden put the unfinished lesson beside the next day's work. The card order
was complete. It could be entered in the week's account; the lesson could wait
for another afternoon. He did not cancel it.

In April Lovelace returned to the office decision. She had not resigned. That possibility had been feared
by both men and would have allowed them to treat her absence as consent obtained
by exhaustion. Instead she took a sheet of the venture's paper and wrote a
qualification beneath the February decision.

The 1851 trial established one frozen operation under prospective comparison,
not the rate at which customer work could be prepared and independently
checked. The four obligations depended upon capacity not present when they were
accepted.

She signed and dated it.","textSha256":"6c2c173d27ff24c61d938954e2f8a3ff2ec1bb6f7684085829e2242451f632b6"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.10.scene.01","text":"## X. The Unfunded Successor

By August, Lovelace could work for an hour and lose the afternoon to it.

The arithmetic of her illness was more exact than its cause. A journey to
London spent several days. A long letter spent one. Visitors spent whatever
strength courtesy concealed from them. At Ockham, papers from the Calculation
Office arrived in packets whose urgency was visible before she broke their
seals.

William found her with the capacity qualification, Neale's checking sheets, and
three letters spread over the bed.

“You promised me one hour,” he said.

“I said I would not travel.”

“You promised both.”

He removed none of the papers. He set the water within her reach and drew the
curtains against the light.

“They have made checking depend upon a single man,” she said.

“Then it does not depend upon you.”

“It depends upon my continuing to insist that he is single.”

Her signature stood alone beside the claim clauses in the copy before her.
Beneath it, *deputy, if required* was still legible through the line she had
drawn. She set one finger on it.

“Would you have signed it?” she asked.

“What?”

“If they had put your name there.”

“I could not have done your work.”

“No.”

She drew the copy back onto her lap. A moment later she straightened it so he
could read the line.

“I would not have let you,” she said.

William sat down beside the bed. She waited for him to say that she had been
right. He asked whether the water was still cool.

Wills still learned from Neale between preparations. She had proposed taking
him off that work for part of each week: some time under Neale, some with an
assurance clerk outside the office. His absence from the preparation desk would
have to be paid for as well as the instruction. During training, output would
fall further. The additional wages and external review would cost approximately one
hundred and twenty pounds in the first year. Halden's answer praised the plan
and asked whether it might begin after the four current packets were delivered.
Babbage's answer proposed that recurrent portions of comparison might later be
mechanized.

She read Halden's answer again, looking for a date she could put beside the
cost. Babbage offered a route through machinery that did not yet exist. Neither paper gave her a day when Wills's hours would be reserved for the instruction.

Lovelace began another page with three headings: competence, paid time,
authority to refuse. She entered Wills, Neale, Halden, Babbage, Davies, and
herself. No row was complete. She sent the unfinished table to both men and
asked them to accept no work beyond Neale's demonstrated reach until one was.","textSha256":"e80e5f0e0786d73ed7f94ceada474214b80d204dd967ced9aa5a4d1a3108697a"},{"nodeId":"document.book.07r2.chapter.10.scene.02","text":"Babbage came to Ockham near the end of the month. He brought drawings rather
than the office account. She recognized the peace offering and the evasion in
the same roll of paper.

He opened the roll across her unanswered table. She drew one edge of it back
into view.

He showed her a proposed means by which a later apparatus might verify parts of
its own operation sequence.

She followed his pencil through two transfers and made him return to the carry.
At the next comparison she stopped him again: both checking paths inherited the
same earlier value. He stared at the lines, rubbed one away with his thumb, and
sent the second path through another register. She moved the delayed sign one
operation farther. He saw why before she explained it.

She left one finger where the two paths had inherited the same value. “If a
later apparatus compared enough of its own operations, would you call that
judgment?”

“Judgment is often the name we give an operation whose conditions have not yet
been exposed,” he said. “If the apparatus compares its own proceedings and
changes what follows, at what exact line would you deny it the word?”

“I wrote that an Engine might compose music if the relations of harmony could
be given to its operations. It might carry them to a passage no composer had
set down note by note.”

“Would it not have invented the passage?”

“The consequence might be new to us. The relations and purpose would still
have entered from us. Our surprise would not be its intention.”

He crossed out *verification* and wrote *comparison of internal operations*.

For several minutes the mechanism occupied the whole table. He began a mark and
she completed it; she crossed out his correction and he laughed. Their old
speed returned so suddenly that neither acknowledged it. For those minutes
William's hour ceased to exist for both of them. Then she reached for the
pencil and had to wait for her breath. When she shifted in the chair, the edge
of Guardian's source sheet slipped from beneath the roll.

“It is good,” she said.

He waited for the rest.

“It does not read Guardian's source sheet.”

She drew the successor register from beneath the roll and closed it over his
letter.

He did not consent or refuse. He recommended that the office wait. Halden
adopted the recommendation, deferring the paid release and outside instruction
until the present contracts produced their next payments.

After he left, Lovelace attached his answer and Halden's to her question. She
left the page unclosed, so the unanswered place remained visible.","textSha256":"ac28b8bb098acc52435ac0bb0c2983cf9897da0ba0b0f5fd03b00e943cee504f"}],"proposal":"Ground the four assessment carrier descriptions in E20 and distinguish the coarse succession assessment from a uniform moment-by-moment emotional trajectory. No replacement numerical values are proposed without a substantive reason.","limits":"Only six Cuts are under content review.
