{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"# Independent comparison: The Book of Conditions

This is a **labeled before/after comparison, not a blind reading**. I read the complete `book/baseline.md` (11,719 words) followed by the complete `book/candidate-v1.md` (11,677 words), then inspected their diff to locate changes. I did not consult other reviews, model records, or agent notes. References below use candidate line numbers unless otherwise specified. This is a literary assessment, not a historical or technical fact check.

## Overall judgment

**Prefer the candidate after two localized repairs.** It is a modest, real improvement, principally in scene causality and the final father–son exchange. Most of the prose, and most of its strengths, are inherited unchanged. It does not substantially reinvent or differentiate the voices. Its best edits remove a second explanation after a scene has already made its point; its best addition lets a character cause a failure that the baseline largely summarized.

The substantial new scene in IX earns its space. The replacement in XI, immediately before the closure resolution, does not: it removes useful mixed motives and introduces an unclear accounting gesture at the moment a consequential decision needs to be legible. Chapter X also needs two short continuity adjustments because training is now explicitly underway.

Confidence is high in those local judgments and moderate in the overall preference. The candidate was read second, so recognition may make its shortened passages feel more sufficient than they would to a new reader. It is therefore significant that the knowledge supporting most cuts is also present earlier within the candidate itself. I would not describe this as a large improvement in overall literary quality.

## Keep

1. **IX: the interrupted lesson (1207–1226).** This is the clearest improvement. Halden has promised, “We begin training now,” and the candidate lets him keep the promise in form while defeating it in practice:

   > “The cards first, Wills. Then come back.”

   > By the time the cards were ready, Neale's paid hours for that day were over.

   The causal sequence is comprehensible without an explanatory speech: urgent production consumes the hours intended to create future capacity. “Another preparer would have to learn the arrangement” gives Halden a plausible local reason, so the scene is more than a demonstration that he is wrong. His familiar ruler and pencil leave with Wills; Neale leaves the specimen in place. Those separate actions make the interrupted relationship tangible.

   Keep “He did not cancel it.” Its position after the completed card order lets the sentence register as Halden's defense of himself. It adds ambiguity about his self-understanding without concealing what he did. The passage makes the later delivery exception an escalation of an observed habit, rather than only the consequence of an abstract capacity calculation.

2. **XII: the shorter Babbage concession (1607–1617).** Prefer:

   > “The distinction was true.”

   > Henry waited.

   > “But they bought the table,” Charles said.

   The baseline recapitulates the machine/office distinction twice, including “The office had undertaken to deliver a correct table.” The candidate keeps Babbage's need to defend the truth of his distinction, then makes his concession an effort he reaches after Henry waits. The plain final sentence works because it is a departure from his habitual argumentative precision. The surrounding drawing exchange and “Of that object … Not of the Engine” preserve his resistance; this is not a conversion speech. Removing his explicit tribute to Lovelace here loses a little overt recognition, but her surviving qualification and the last physical arrangement of the papers carry her importance without reinstating the recap.

3. **VI: Lovelace's response to the failed assembly (712–716).** The candidate asks:

   > Could Farrow state a new tolerance for the shared drive and inspect it?

   and admits:

   > She could not tell from the report whether Babbage's design would prove the better machine.

   This is more convincingly a practical answer from an absent person than the baseline's lesson about parts satisfying “local conditions” and failing “in composition.” The conditional question establishes what can be tried while preserving uncertainty over which design is superior. It also keeps Lovelace from becoming the narrator's infallible mouthpiece. “Neither proposal had yet turned the handle” belongs to this narrator's material vocabulary and leads naturally to Halden's unsuccessful attempt to move it. Preserve the later recognition that Babbage's untried improvement might still be better.

4. **IX: the date and agency of the capacity entry (1065–1066).** “In February 1852, Halden entered eighty hours” provides an unobtrusive temporal anchor before the 1854 delivery schedule, and identifies the estimate as his undertaking. The baseline postpones naming the decision's year until much later. The date improves orientation without inserting an explanatory digression.

5. **IX: compressing the decision summary (1199–1205).** “Neither could sign a customer's acceptance for Halden” and the four dated acceptances are enough to place responsibility. The baseline's explicit three-way ballot and restatement of all authorities make the scene stop to pronounce its own result. The candidate preserves the voices already heard in debate and then moves into the hand signing the papers. Lovelace's request to record her objection is useful action, not merely a narrated category of dissent.

6. **IV: the shorter ending (517–518).** Keep the cut of “A customer had refused to buy a vision. A works had refused to price unsupported precision.” Both refusals have already been enacted. The total at the end is still characteristic of Halden and the narrator. The cut gives the chapter a cleaner exit; it does not need a replacement moral.

7. **V: the shortened authority paragraph (578–580).** Keep the concrete limits of her signature and the household constraint. The removed “one bounded consequence to an authority that the surrounding world did not give her generally” restates what the surrounding social and contractual details let us see. Crucially, keep the entire deputy scene preceding this paragraph: “Chosen by whom?” and her striking out the provision make her later admission to William complicated and earned.

8. **XII: the shortened final inventory (1683–1685).** Slight preference for the candidate. “Side by side” already supplies the equality that “equally preserved” explains. The seal and its date are not needed for orientation at this point. The repeated widening handwriting and the final act of tying remain, preserving both emotional and material continuity. This is a small gain, not a reason by itself to prefer a version.

## Revise before acceptance

**X: complete the training distinction (1290–1301 and 1360–1361).** Keep the added distinction between learning “between preparations” and protected time away from preparation. It makes Lovelace's proposal concrete and explains why the proposed expenditure is additional. But the unchanged sentence:

> Neither paper gave her a day on which Wills would begin.

now momentarily contradicts the immediately preceding statement that he “still learned from Neale,” as well as the new March scene. Likewise, “deferring training until the present contracts produced their next payments” can sound as though all training has been suspended, although the candidate has carefully established something more specific.

Change only the referents: the missing date should be the date Wills would be released from preparation for the proposed instruction; the deferred commitment should be that allocation of paid time. There is no need to explain the whole distinction again. The new scene supplies the explanation. This is a high-confidence continuity repair, not a request for another scene.

## Reject this replacement; preserve the useful motive

**XI: the new paragraph before the closure resolution (1476–1477).** The candidate substitutes:

> New money might keep Wills and Neale employed. Halden left room for it in the account, below the sums Margaret had asked him to pay first.

for the baseline's temptation, which includes “preserve Halden's standing” and the risk of presenting a disclosed failure as proof that the system has already corrected itself.

“Left room for it” is too indeterminate here. Is he budgeting on another subscription, keeping open the option of reopening, or merely leaving blank space? The next sentence is “He wrote the closure resolution.” That jump obscures the decision rather than leaving a productive uncertainty about the man. The account is described immediately above as unable to sustain the remaining work; the new gesture does not tell us what has resolved his temptation to raise more capital.

The cut also gives his temptation only the benevolent motive of keeping Wills and Neale employed. The lost interest in preserving his own standing matters: Halden can do the responsible thing while still wishing to save his reputation. This is consistent with his earlier pleasure at being called an inventor and with Wills having to prompt a fuller reference after the supposedly complete closure account.

Do not necessarily restore all five baseline lines. Its last sentence, about having spent twelve years teaching others, is an explicit moral summation and can go. **Retain the mixed motive and a legible refusal of the proposed circular; reject the ambiguous “left room for it” action.** The immediately preceding imagined circular and Margaret's question already carry much of the reasoning. A shorter paragraph can preserve “New money might preserve Halden's standing and keep Wills and Neale employed” without giving up the candidate's restraint.

## Distinctive voices and passages to protect

The narrator has a recognizable intelligence: dry wit, exact institutional detail, and the tendency to locate an abstraction in an object or a paid hour. “The mechanism's resistance entered Farrow's life first as Friday” and “Monday had filled itself before it arrived” belong to that voice. Do not strip all judgments or aphorisms merely because some of the candidate's deletions work. The revisions succeed where an immediately preceding scene has already supplied the insight.

Babbage remains expansive, defensive about the exact extent of a finding, and unable to leave a drawing alone. Halden speaks in wages, dates, and quantities, but borrows Babbage's confidence when it suits him. Lovelace answers with sharply bounded questions and can be possessive about the authority she has won. Those distinctions survive the candidate; they are not newly created by it. Their shared tendency to deliver polished antitheses is still noticeable, so I would not claim that this pass has solved all voice convergence. Additional ornamental verbal quirks would not help.

The smaller voices are often the most individually persuasive. Preserve Margaret's “Let me finish this line,” the subsequent muddle over the two brothers in her novel, and William's choice to ask whether the water is cool instead of endorsing Ada's self-justification. They give these people attention and desires outside the venture's argument. Preserve Davies's “Before or after I pay?” and Neale's “Nor can I … Leave it open.” Their economy distinguishes them from the principal debaters.

Above all, retain Wills's reference scene unchanged. “Not the copying … I did that” and “Only the other part as well” make him neither an abstract victim nor a mouthpiece for institutional responsibility. Halden taking a fresh sheet instead of writing small is earned by the pressure between them. The candidate wisely leaves this alone. Also preserve the three purposeless strokes after the successful test and the shared drawing at Ockham: these moments let delight coexist with the errors the narrative investigates.

The candidate's strongest change therefore concerns **how the failure happens**, with a smaller improvement to how Babbage can acknowledge it. Its chief risk is treating explicitness as inherently undesirable: the XI replacement demonstrates that a material gesture can still be less clear and less psychologically rich than a short statement of competing motives.

{"id": "story.fact.book.restart.20260927", "chapter": 8, "claim": "A first attempt fails to clear, is stopped, and the complete run starts over.", "event_id": "event.book.07r2.E14a", "path": "/description", "evidence": {"node_id": "document.book.07r2.chapter.08.scene.01", "quote": "At the sixth, one register failed to clear completely. Halden called the stop
before anyone could decide that the remaining digit was harmless. The card was
marked and the incomplete run was voided. Davies had already leaned toward the
glass. Irritation crossed his face before he told one clerk to note the card and
the other to leave the locked case shut. Under observation the register was
reset, the inputs were restored, and the full twelve-case sequence began again
from its first declared card. The interruption entered the trace; it was not
smuggled into either accepted run. Babbage objected to losing the completed
cases and then, seeing Davies watch him, objected to nothing further."}, "reader_first_known": {"nodeId": "document.book.07r2.chapter.08.scene.01", "boundary": "end"}, "epistemic_status": "authored_fiction", "assertion_scope": "Only this separate fact, not every fact in the native Event, becomes disclosed here."}

# Understanding notes for the editable world model

These are concise records of consequential authoring judgments. They are not
hidden reasoning transcripts, historical evidence, or story passages. Each
note points to the world decision it explains and may be superseded when the
world is revised.

nodes.text:
## U01 — Why a third principal exists

Targets: E02--E06; Edward Halden's life.

Babbage and Lovelace can continue a negotiation but cannot, between them,
supply independent manufacture, commercial staging, and liability. The third
principal therefore carries the narrow integration function that makes the
divergence causal. He is fictional because assigning all of that function to a
known historical figure would distort the evidence. He does not absorb the
manufacturer, customer, financier, or successor roles.
nodes.title: U01 — Why a third principal exists

nodes.text:
## U02 — Why the machine is small

Targets: the Bounded Card Apparatus; E03, E06, E14.

A completed general Analytical Engine by 1851 would require far more
counterfactual industrial change than the story needs. A six-register,
addition-and-subtraction, card-directed apparatus gives the founders something
real to finish and test while preserving the distinction between the bounded
artifact and Babbage's architecture. If later technical opening shows even this
configuration to be implausible, reduce its registers or card sequence rather
than enlarging the industrial world to rescue it.
nodes.title: U02 — Why the machine is small

nodes.text:
## U03 — Why success is the central shock

Targets: E14--E18.

Another mechanical failure would merely confirm every existing caution. A
bounded success changes the principals' wants and interpretations in different
directions and creates the temptation the conditions were designed to resist.
It therefore produces both stronger causality and a better story: their method
works, then they misstate what its success licenses.
nodes.title: U03 — Why success is the central shock

nodes.text:
## U04 — Why the office fails outside the mechanism

Targets: E17--E27.

The tested arithmetic should remain true. The office fails because recurring
calculation is a human-machine process containing preparation, checking,
delivery, correction, and money. The known two-job checking capacity, the
four-job commitment, the specific transposition, and the omitted duplicate
check make the failure traceable without making the apparatus magically break
at the required dramatic moment.

nodes.text:
## U05 — Why Lovelace's death is not the cause of the error

Targets: E19--E24.

Her illness and death expose a succession failure already visible in the 1852
capacity review. The surviving principals choose not to fund a second checker
before she dies. Death removes her active pressure; it does not enter a wrong
number or force Halden's later delivery decision. This preserves agency and
avoids using a woman's death as a mechanical plot device.
nodes.title: U05 — Why Lovelace's death is not the cause of the error

nodes.text:
## U06 — Why the ending is documentary

Targets: E27--E30.

The counterfactual earns one bounded proof, not an industrial revolution. The
complete packet is a meaningful surviving object because it contains success
and failure under the same identity. Babbage's late growth is the decision not
to curate away the parts that limit his preferred interpretation.

nodes.text:
## U07 — Revision from the first candidate round

Targets: the whole 07r2 construction.

The earlier candidate passes showed that a plausible macro outcome was not enough:
continued negotiation lacked a person capable of converting it into priced,
staged obligations. This version retains the useful bounded-proof and
overcommitment pattern, adds the missing commercial founder, and narrows the
long-run outcome. Discarded casts, signature objects, prose, and numerical
worlds are not part of this construction.

nodes.text:
## U08 — Pragmatic revision rule

Targets: all later openings.

When a finer event is uncertain but does not change the parent account, keep it
coarse or put it in the remainder. When a local route is weak, repair that
route. When the children reveal that the parent could not have happened, or
that the only coherent realization is dramatically inert, revise the parent
and propagate the change. Do not restart a whole world to avoid making an
ordinary authorial choice.

nodes.text:
## U09 — Why this world is accepted

Targets: the complete macro, E01--E30, and the twelve-passage route.

Progressive opening found local defects—the access route to Halden, the formal
authority behind the 1852 contracts, and the exact 1854 delivery choice—but no
failure of the parent history. Farrow now supplies the access route, Halden
alone binds the customers after Babbage urges expansion, and the omitted check
has its own Direction Cut. The ledgers close, the prospective test remains
valid, and each principal's late action grows out of an earlier pattern. The
world is therefore accepted at its declared resolution. Unopened workshop,
subscriber, and customer detail stays remainder rather than delaying the book.
nodes.title: U09 — Why this world is accepted

nodes.text:
## U10 — Why assurance and threat are separated from fear

Targets: the principal period profiles; selected-scene WHAT and FEELS Cuts;
passages I--XII.

The five core wants identify what is receiving motivational attention. They do
not by themselves say whether the person expects those wanted endpoints to be
secured. The added outlook Cut therefore divides one comparable unit between
assured fulfillment, threatened fulfillment, and unresolved expectation; its
threat child may then be opened across the five wanted regions. Fear remains a
separate emotional appraisal because the same represented threat can instead
organize anger, sadness, bargaining, or action. This distinction guided a
small rendering revision: Babbage classifies mechanisms under threat,
Lovelace converts uncertainty into explicit conditions, and Halden moves from
bounded accounting through promotional accounting to self-audit. No world
event or causal dependency changed.

nodes.text:
## U11 — Why the emotional-depth pass adds residue rather than shocks

Targets: E09--E11, E14, E18--E28; passages II, V, VII--XII.

The accepted world already contains the required long perturbations: earlier
institutional rupture makes finite dependence threatening to Babbage; bounded
success destabilizes both him and Halden; Lovelace's foreseeable absence tests
whether authority has a carrier; and the returned table forces a slow change in
what counts as the work's complete record. Adding another catastrophe would
weaken that causality. The revision instead repeats existing objects with
changed use—drawings cover ledgers, deposit letters cover the capacity line,
handwriting widens, checking tools wear, and proof and failure remain under one
tape. Explanatory prose was removed where those residues could show adaptation.
nodes.title: U11 — Why the emotional-depth pass adds residue rather than shocks

nodes.text:
## U12 — Why character refinements change the model before the rendering

Targets: E04, E06, E09, E14, E17, E20, and E26; passages II--XII.

Lovelace's fallibility and the secondary people's lives need consequences beyond
their assigned jobs. The smallest correction does not add a new shock. It opens consequences
already latent in accepted Events. In the finite compact Lovelace declines an
unspecified deputy because substitution could dissolve the rare authority she
has won; in 1852 she recognizes that this protection also made her a single
carrier, which sharpens rather than magically supplies her succession argument.
Davies's curiosity makes evidential restraint a choice, Farrow protects his
foreman's finding despite delayed payment, and Neale tries to teach Wills
without counting supervised practice as independent capacity, then shares
responsibility for the correction. These refinements were entered in the life
and Event descriptions before their passages were revised. They do not alter
the macro outcome or any existing Cut composition. The remaining changes remove
balanced, thesis-bearing speech and replace it with handling, interruption, and
profession-specific language; those are rendering changes rather than new
world facts.
nodes.title: U12 — Why character refinements change the model before the rendering

## U13 — Why invention joy is deepened

Targets: E03, E10, E14, E16, and E18; the finite-invention and
recognition-to-overreach change arcs; passages III, VI, VIII--X.

The rendering moves too quickly from making to governance.
The repair therefore opens experiences already causal in the accepted world.
Halden's reversal from pricing a machine part to pricing an answerable claim is
treated as a cognitive invention; the corrected assembly's first free motion is
allowed to reward several kinds of expertise; and the successful trial is
experienced as shared joy before commercial attention arrives.

The pleasure is not an ornamental scene. E14 changes beliefs about feasibility,
standing, and the value of each participant's work. E16 reinforces those
beliefs. In E18 Babbage and Halden then mistake two judgments moved by the same
success and response for independent confirmation. This was already the
recognition-to-overreach arc; the revision makes its positive shock perceptible.
That common-cause account belongs to the constructor's model and is not given to
Lovelace as an explicit diagnosis in the rendered scene. She can demonstrate
the capacity error without possessing the whole explanation of either man.
Accordingly, only the three immediate post-trial FEELS Cuts change. Their joy
shares rise and their anticipatory shares fall because the named moment is now
fixed after the second complete run and before the first inquiry. WHAT, HOW,
fulfillment outlook, threat, and Direction Cuts remain unchanged.

The same macro history and failure remain. The revision develops four literary
functions—cognitive discovery, pleasure in matter,
shared recognition, and intellectual intimacy under bodily cost—through the
current model's existing Events, relationships, Cuts, and change arcs.

## U14 — Why Lovelace discusses mechanical judgment

Targets: E20 and E20a; E23--E26 and E28; passage X; the valid-computational-claim
concept model.

Lovelace's published 1843 Notes already distinguish the Engine's ability to
follow supplied analytical relations from any power to originate those
relations, while also proposing that suitably represented relations outside
ordinary number—including harmony—could be subjected to operation. Passage X
does not quote the Notes or attribute modern terminology to her. It develops
those documented positions inside the counterfactual self-comparison design.

The exchange changes a record: a common-source fault causes Babbage to narrow
mechanical verification to comparison of internal operations. Lovelace states
only the distinction between an unforeseen consequence and intention.
Guardian's source sheet, followed by the returned table, supplies the adverse
case.

## U15 — Why voice and sensory detail are consequences of the model

Targets: principal life trajectories; E03, E06, E10, E14, E18, E20--E21, and E26;
passages I--XI.

The voice pass adds no Event, Cut, causal dependency, or outcome. Sentence
movement and diction are derived from the person's existing organization:
Babbage expands from the local question toward architecture, Lovelace translates
between representations and grows terser as bodily capacity declines, and
Halden names hours, money, workers, dates, and deliverables. Secondary voices
use the narrower evidence their work makes available. These are rendering
constraints recorded in `PERSON-MODELS.md`, not new personality coordinates.

Sensory detail is likewise rendered from Things already participating in an
Event and from their changing state: coupled assemblies transmit load, heat,
and vibration; the trial exposes cards, register faces, the slowing shaft, and
the sealed comparison case; the succession episode exposes drawings, breath,
packets, and the cold apparatus. A city or room remains a Place Thing; presence
and any consequential weather, traffic, work, or crowd condition are Events in
its lifecycle. A separate place Event is opened only if that condition changes
access, timing, choice, or consequence. This keeps atmosphere available without
letting an unmodeled detail become a hidden cause.

The final bounded prose pass opens the already recorded deputy refusal and
its later recognition, without adding a successor or changing the plot.
Lovelace hesitates before striking the provision; in illness she asks William
about the signature and admits she would have refused his substitution.
Recognition does not settle her attachment to the authority she secured.
Several narrator explanations are removed where the action already supplies
their meaning, and a few exchanges lose their immediate polished rebuttals.
E06, E20, the person description, and the route retain those same choices.
The Cut weights, accounting, dates, capacity, outcomes, and ending are
unchanged. A fresh retrospective import is required to bind the revised
descriptions and manuscript to their new source identities.

## U16 - Connect preparation to the final checking window

Targets: E09, E17--E18, E22--E24; passages VI, IX, and X.

A fresh complete-manuscript reading identified a missing link: at forty hours
per packet, four checks appear finishable long before the 1854 delivery unless
the reader knows why the final inputs are not yet available. The world model
already placed all four checks in one delivery quarter. This pass opens that
commitment: methods and specimen work precede customer returns closed at the
end of 1853; final figures arrive in early 1854 for April--June delivery.
Earlier checking cannot certify those new values. This is an authored source
dependency, not a fifth customer, new historical evidence, or new work invented
to consume every intervening hour.

Halden's error remains a gamble on future capacity followed by a refusal to
fund it. The existing 80-hour capacity, 40-hour final check, four contracts,
cash accounts, and decision Cuts are unchanged. The model descriptions and
loadable scaffold request are updated before the prose. The scene then shows
old checking marks being set aside instead of adding a speech about scheduling.

The same reading caught two consecutive Babbage speeches that looked like
alternating speakers in VI. His claim that the failure justifies the larger
redesign is joined into one attributed speech. No character position changes.
The witnessed test, emotional palette, death, closure, and custody ending are
preserved. This pass does not claim a fresh Rust import.

## U17 - Retrospective Rust import and the final-source cutoff

Targets: E17--E24; passages IX--X; the concept component Cut and person scaffolds.

The construction review distinguished a coherent authored artifact from a
complete native execution record. This repair imports the existing descriptions,
person processes, Cuts, and manuscript into a new database. It records the
source digests and new compilation and retrieval results; it does not recover
earlier editing order. The concept allocation gains an explicit zero remainder
and component addresses. All thirteen declared person profiles now request
their nine concurrent processes. Slow outlook remains authored: unselected
scenes are not invented to manufacture a temporal-mixture proof.

Checking the source schedule exposed a remaining causal weakness in U16's
refinement. Returns available during the first quarter could consume that
quarter's checking hours before April--June. The revised authored arrangement
is that customers reconcile the year-end returns during the first quarter,
then release the final signed checking copies from 1 April 1854. Guardian's
copy arrives on that date; other April arrivals remain coarse. Work on earlier
specimens or provisional figures cannot replace comparison against these final
copies. E22's window extends through April, and the model, route, and two
affected passages carry the same constraint.

This supersedes U16's source-availability assumption, not its preserved account
of the earlier revision. The four jobs, forty hours per final check, eighty
protected quarter-hours, omission on 7 April, refund, closure, and ending do
not change. Nor do the psychological weights. The alteration is a local repair
to the causal explanation, not new historical evidence or a rerolled world.

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"interpretation","text":"Authoring interpretation of E28–E29 and Chapter XII, not a claim that Henry inherits a complete theory or can finish the Engine. Henry does not refute the exact mechanism trace. He leaves the returned table between the piles and asks for a heading that accounts for both. Charles first offers an Engine heading and then adds the bounded apparatus and calculation office, including proof, error and closure. The changed question makes a true but incomplete distinction insufficient for this inventory. Henry's custody work participates in that discovery; he is more than a passive recipient of his father's conclusion. Both headings remain. Charles's renewed impatience and 'Keep the sentence' leave the depth and durability of recognition open. Further exploration can ask what the documents let these two people understand together without claiming that their private disagreement is resolved."}
nodes.title: The inventory question changes the object being described

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"interpretation","text":"Authoring interpretation of the current fictional model and passages, not a statement of Margaret's private knowledge. In Chapter VII Margaret finishes her own account line before taking the venture ledger, then asks whether earned wages can actually be paid on Friday. Edward begins an explanation about hoped-for calls; she returns the ledger to the current balance. In Chapter XI she separates debts, cash in hand and a circular's hoped-for receipts. These are a repeated way of making an imagined rescue answerable to a present obligation. Edward already knows the figures; another person's question changes which figures govern his decision. Her own paid work and household exposure matter here. Open next question: why does this available practice fail to constrain the four-deposit decision? The text supports a question about attention and recognition, not an assertion that Margaret foresaw every later choice."}
nodes.title: Margaret changes what Edward must answer

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"interpretation","text":"Authoring interpretation, not knowledge silently assigned to either character. E17 and Chapter IX show Wills starting from an expected answer in a prepared copy, then admitting that the source is unreadable. Neale admits the same limit and leaves the check open. E26 and Chapter XI show Wills initially rushing after correction, then putting his pencil across the copy and audibly asking for an unheard figure; Neale repeats it. Checking here requires both an independent source and an interaction in which uncertainty can stop the work. The later action can be read as a local development from avoiding interruption to making one. It does not prove a completed personality change, add independent checker-hours, or establish that E17's missing original was obtained. Further opening could follow what the strip, role exchange and Neale's response contribute, without adding an incident or score."}
nodes.title: Checking includes permission to interrupt

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"question","text":"What does Wills choose to show a future employer, and can he interrupt when Neale is absent? The model already has a coarse later railway-accounting life, but this scene does not disclose that future or explain its route. Follow that branch only when the story benefits. Margaret’s independent pleasures and Henry’s technical interests remain open inquiries."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Nora’s unsettled_account disposition is realized in a reference that becomes more useful only when its subject asks for a change. The ruler, fresh sheet and second initials make the action material. Wills’s “Only the other part as well” is practical and hesitant; Halden’s “I wasn’t going to take it out” retains defensiveness; Neale attests to witnessed work. This is a modeler’s reading of the prose, not proof of a true voice. Independent reader B found the careful exchange procedural and slower, but coherent and not overexplained. Repeated ruler movements remain a possible pacing cost."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Nora’s care conflict distinguishes an accurate record from permission to decide for another person. This is an authorial analogy to investigate beside the Book’s existing actions, not an identity between the worlds: Babbage’s exact mechanism claim in I and XI does not settle what the office promised, and Lovelace’s deputy refusal in V protects authority while creating a succession vulnerability. Existing U05 and U12 retain their original account. Future revision should preserve each person’s partly valid position and era-specific powers rather than make Nora’s contemporary lesson their shared speech."}
nodes.title: An accurate account can fail to answer another person

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"The ending already names a bounded object: configuration, proof, qualification, error, correction and closure. Nora’s new compositional question is whether faithful custody can leave the people more various than this account of their undertaking. Her own later relapse into planning Kit’s life prevents an easy claim that recognition permanently cures a habit. Preserve Babbage’s impatient last question and Henry’s separate life; do not add a concluding thesis. This is a new interpretation linked to the received ending, not recovered intent."}
nodes.title: Complete of an object, not complete of a person

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Nora’s shoulder adaptation and earlier care fatigue supply sensitivity to changing reach, waiting and ordinary dependence. They do not diagnose Lovelace or alter her historical-counterfactual illness. In Chapter X William’s water, the interrupted pencil and the unclosed page can remain distinct from the professional argument. In IX and XI, Neale and Wills’ checking actions acquire different meanings through their own modeled learning. Future voice review must inspect those processes and actual lines separately."}
nodes.title: Bodily limits alter rhythm without settling meaning

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Nora’s tendency to make family time absorb her jobs makes Chapter VII’s interrupted account especially salient. The existing passage already lets Margaret finish her own line before taking Edward’s book. That is a strength to preserve. A future opening should ask what Margaret attends to before and after the exchange and whether it changes a meaningful choice; adding biography or dialogue merely to make her a lecturer would weaken the scene. This remains an open authorial inquiry, not new world canon."}
nodes.title: Margaret’s work has a life beyond correcting Halden

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Prospective compositional connection, created 27 September 2026. Nora’s fabrication and singing experiences make her attentive to the real pleasure in Chapter VI’s extra turn and Chapter VIII’s three empty strokes after success. These passages already work through action and sensory attention. The new author model is a reason to preserve and explore their distinct pleasures, not to add a moral after them or claim she caused their existing wording. U13 already records the original construction rationale."}
nodes.title: Nora and the pleasure of making

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"“One farther” and “You see” let Charles direct attention in the clipped manner of someone tired but still occupied by his work. Henry’s questions and moving of the sheet show participation without promising succession. Their shared technical interest makes the later “Do you?” less tidily resolved. The custody headings and 1900 survival-only ending stand."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Margaret’s “Don’t go yet” asks for company after the existing account discussion. “Only one of them has the estate” is a joke inside their reading, not another principle she teaches Edward. Edward’s interrupted errand and dry reply preserve his preoccupation and a small capacity for company. No permanent change in his financial judgment is inferred. The older current-balance note still stands; its question about the later failure remains open."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Self-review of the exact final prose. “She began a paragraph earlier” leaves shared pleasure as an activity; the discarded “this time he listened” would have turned it into Edward’s lesson. In XII hands move paper before the inventory argument resumes. These choices realize Nora’s attention to pleasure and physical reach without making her modern biography historical evidence or retroactively crediting her with the prior book."}

Keep proposals distinct from accepted model facts. Store scene drafts before review, including rejected alternatives; scene_commit stores the reviewed story text. Record purpose-review outcomes and deliberate suspense/disclosure processes in the graph. After narrative revision, update the graph and export the rendered text again; never patch the exported manuscript independently. Tool validation checks structure and references, not whether every unwritten thought was recorded or every literary judgment is correct.\nRecord as you write, not only at milestones: ideas for later scenes, predictions, questions, decisions, references back and voice or phrasing choices (why a line sounds like its speaker) are life_story_author_record kinds idea, prediction, question, decision, reference and voice. Link each to the passages it concerns and, with about, to the model records it concerns (event:, cut:, process:, referent:), so a later agent sees the thought beside its subject. Record every outside review, from a blind reader, another model, an estimator or a person, with life_review_record under its actual reviewer, and link the changes that answer it with answers. Give every Event that carries a Cut a description; scene preparation blocks commits until it has one. From the first exploration of a story, consider the processes of its telling as well as the events it tells. Follow how anticipation, dramatic pressure, rhythm, attention, humor, intimacy, disclosure or a process you discover changes as the text unfolds. Ask what produces a change, what it changes in the meaning of earlier passages, and what remains open. These are invitations to recursive exploration, not required tracks, a prescribed dramatic arc, or a reason to remove quietness and pleasure. Let exploratory writing alter this account and let the account suggest new writing. Review actual prose before treating an intended effect as achieved.\nAutomatically consider disclosure when preparing or revising prose: what can the reader already know, what particular facts does this passage reveal, and what remains withheld or ambiguous? Keep this separate from what each focal character knows in world time. A renders link says which Event is depicted, not that all its facts or motives are disclosed. Select small fact/context nodes and give scene.context their explicit readerKnownAt and viewpointKnownAt assignments; do not substitute an entire Event, life dossier or author biography for those facts.\nWhen a delayed reveal, perspective difference, setup or reinterpretation matters, store its plan with life_story_author_record kind disclosure, linked to the actual passages and fact/model records. Use existing stable passage identities, reading order and optional document.span boundaries through life_document_project. No new clock system, book-as-Thing or numerical reader psychology is required. Keep an ordinary scene simple; there is no quota of secrets, fact nodes, subscenes or suspense values. If no special withholding or timing matters, say why the existing treatment suffices in the review rather than inventing a plot device.\nWhen useful to inspect a telling process across passages, store an authored qualitative account with life_story_author_record kind assessment. Its optional data convention is {schema:\"meaning-model-document-process/v1\",documentId:storyRootId,label,question,summary,states:[{label,spanId,description,evidence:[{nodeId,excerpt}]}]}. Choose your own process labels and meaningful phases, using existing document.span IDs and exact quotations inside those spans. The tool records explicit about-links and the reviewed passage identities; the viewer shows these phases under Reading position → Story processes. Create a span through ordinary narrative records when a useful extent has none. Reading position is this document's ordered text, not elapsed world time, the author's life, or the authoring_step clock. The phase boundaries follow their passages as text length changes. Qualitative states need no numeric tension score. If numbers serve a specific question, declare whose judgment they are, comparison anchors, units and uncertainty through the existing numerical grammar; do not imply measured reader psychology or invent a generating law.\nAfter splitting, merging, moving or changing a passage, inspect the affected telling and disclosure plans against the new text and reading order. Parent connections may remain with the container; relink a narrower disclosure explicitly when it belongs to a child. Stable anchors follow text extents, but do not prove the revised prose still has the same effect. A changed phase is marked for review; record a fresh assessment linked with supersedes when it replaces an earlier one. Investigate new questions recursively, including promising discoveries without a defect; these questions are starting points, not an exhaustive recipe. The model and its Understanding Graph are your understanding: what is not recorded cannot be picked up by a later agent, and a thought not linked to what it concerns is lost. Give every Event that carries a Cut a description of what happens in it, and describe most other Events. Record your choices, ideas, predictions, questions, voice and phrasing decisions and their reasons with life_understanding_record, linked to the records and nodes they concern. Record every outside review, from another model, a blind reader, an estimator or a person, with life_review_record under its actual reviewer, and link later changes that answer it with answers. Before you report to the user, put every reason you give there into the graph: a later agent reads the graph, not your reply. To continue existing work, read life_construction_replay from the start at outline level, then life_model_outline, and open detail where you need it.\n\nAcross core modeling, storytelling, and ideation, explore recursively from the question and the model: follow discoveries into relevant subprocesses, competing accounts, missing relationships, or better representations, then reconsider the whole. Use existing grammar and stable record identities; distinguish what exists or happens, who believes or proposes it, and what a particular representation communicates. Keep evidence, attribution, uncertainty, and unresolved questions visible. Add physical placement, movement, reach, or access when they affect a consequential interaction; use a declared reference frame and units when numerical coordinates serve that question. A region name or an attachment alone does not establish a spatial relationship. Distinguish qualitative places and relations, declared numerical positions, and evaluated movement in both the model and your report. When the user needs a physical view or spatial reasoning, model the useful geometry: source real geography with appropriate precision and distinguish a representative town point from a building; author fictional room layouts or movements when delegated and label them as invented, not historical measurements. Give a place a stable identity distinct from a scene or journey; separate locations before assigning positions. Declare frame origin, axis order, units, time applicability, provenance and uncertainty; do not combine local frames or latitude/longitude with metric distances without an explicit transformation. Native object_pose or vector/scalar processes with scale.semantic_role position express numerical placement; bind the process to its subject using coordinate with role position, and declare axes (a scalar also needs scale.axis or one axis). Use located_in for equivalent Event-to-place setting bindings while preserving meaningful roles; this is a reusable convention in an open vocabulary, not a new grammar restriction. Read depth.spatial in life_model_questions for recognized declarations and missing details; it does not certify geography, complete geometry or later motion. For a life or process whose movement matters, begin with its coarse spatial course and deepen selected scenes within it: connect dated bases, workplaces, visits and transitions to the same enduring subject, preserving unknown periods. A landmark coordinate or an isolated room snapshot does not supply that history. A home or work base is not continuous bodily presence, and a sequence of locations is not an observed travel route. Connect physical conditions to the model’s understanding when consequential: who can see, reach, enter, hide, learn or act there, whose interpretation this is, and what remains unknown. Use typed Event/process/subject links and Understanding about-links so these connections remain inspectable. Native position scales may declare spatial_status coarse_life_location, location_role home_base/workplace/visit/presence, place_ref and a concise label; these are open descriptive conventions, not extra engine types or requirements for every subject. Add useful detail and record why it matters or why the current resolution is sufficient; do not require a story, an author persona, numerical psychology, coordinates, or a fixed inventory of categories in every model. These are shared reasoning practices, not claims that the server has independently understood or completed the model.\n\nControlled read-back: at a meaningful milestone, or after a change that could alter what an output conveys, evaluate a bounded selection when conveying model information matters to the task. Prepare this comparison as part of your work; do not wait for the user to ask for a special test. This is not required after every paragraph or tool call. Select the material and the relevant questions before seeing reader responses. Fix a small answer key against the exact model revision, with source record or node references, accepted answers, attribution, uncertainty, and any ambiguity or withholding that should remain. Use neutral extraction questions that do not supply the answer. Test intended disclosures or claims, not recovery of everything in the model.\n\nGive independent blind readers separate packets: the passage or other selected output plus its preceding context and questions, and a control with the same preceding context and questions but without the selected material. Neither packet includes the model, answer key, author notes, future material, or other readers' responses. Keep the answer key outside both packets. Use separate fresh readers for the two conditions; a reader who has seen the selected material cannot supply its blind control. Tell readers they may answer unknown or ambiguous rather than invent an answer. When independent readers are unavailable, label self-review or informed review honestly and leave the independent comparison pending; never fabricate a reader, control, or result.\n\nEvaluate both responses against the fixed key. Report absolute read-back fidelity separately from improvement over the control, with the tested items and denominators visible. A correctly conveyed fact counts toward fidelity even when the control already knew or inferred it; it adds little incremental recovery. Distinguish incorrect claims, unsupported additions, unresolved ambiguity, and missing information; absence is not falsehood. Preserve attributed beliefs as beliefs and deliberate uncertainty as uncertainty. A small test supports only its selected questions, not a verdict on the whole work. Fidelity is not aesthetic quality: do not maximize disclosure, remove useful ambiguity, impose score quotas, or flatten voice, rhythm, and discovery to improve a score.\n\nRecord the plan, fixed targets, exact material identifiers or hashes, relevant model revision, prompts, actual reviewer identities, responses, and separate results through life_understanding_record and life_review_record. Keep private targets and author knowledge out of reader packets. Link any resulting changes to the findings they answer; retain failures and unresolved questions so the next agent can continue the comparison.\n\nRespect the human author's starting brief and chosen involvement. For a new story, ask about unresolved initial settings and writing-process involvement separately; reuse explicit preferences and delegation. Offer setting all or some parameters or delegating them, and autonomous work, selected checkpoints, ongoing collaboration, or a custom arrangement. Read life-sim://addon/storytelling for intake guidance. Automatic modeling and reviews operate within that agreement. Wait for the human at agreed approval checkpoints; saving a proposal or passing a review is not their approval. A bounded review or edit request does not require a new-project questionnaire.\n\nWithin the agreed delegation, review numerical meaning and conceptual depth without waiting for the user to suggest them. Consider authored judgment scales for relevant meanings, motives, capacities or process changes that are not directly measured; define their comparison, units, anchors and uncertainty, and preserve source measurements separately. Open important concepts into useful parts or alternative lenses using native concepts and abstract cuts, then deepen a child when its label does not explain the relevant behavior or distinction. Assess how meanings differ across dates, actors or contexts; distinguish a changing world from a changed estimate, viewpoint or rubric. Store these assessments as Understanding Nodes linked to the actual definitions and evidence. Revisit them after consequential findings or revisions. Explain adequate boundaries, missing evidence or deliberate exclusions; do not invent scores, change or detail just to fill a checklist.\n\nExplore the model recursively throughout the work: opening a process, relationship or meaning can reveal new questions and distinctions, and following them can change the account that first prompted the exploration. Curiosity, surprise, play and discoveries in provisional prose are valid reasons to open the model even when no gap is known. Return to connected regions as understanding changes; the supplied checks do not bound what can be investigated.\nAutomatically review model depth before preparing scenes for commitment and after consequential changes to lives, mechanisms, institutions, causal transitions, outcomes, or disclosure plans. Exploratory candidates, drafts and questions can be saved before this review and while it has unresolved findings; use what they reveal to guide further modeling. Use life_story_model_depth_review with the current story graph, overall-life dossier, a stored outline/plan as focusNodeId, and the relevant contextNodeIds. Read the actual model bound to this graph; model depth cannot be judged from a synopsis or node count alone.\nSupply modelEvidenceRefs for the actual lives, circumstances, constraints and choices the focus depends on, also when a life dossier is present. The packet includes these records and model records anchored by the selected graph nodes. It follows only those explicit references, not every possible explanatory connection: inspect the records, follow relevant dependencies through life_meaning_query or life_model_inspect, and add missing context before concluding. Read every relevant omitted record through the supplied routes; a model summary, dossier, or lens interpretation cannot substitute for its underlying evidence.\nFor an existing work whose lives and causes already live in native model records, explicitly set lifeTrendsNodeId:null and supply modelEvidenceRefs rather than inventing a dossier or duplicating the model into fixed phases. Inspect the returned records and open further evidence through life_meaning_query or life_model_inspect as needed. Judge whether those records explain the chosen focus, and report unknown history or inadequate coverage honestly; references are not proof of a complete life model. This mode supports existing-work review and explicit revision. It does not satisfy the separate life-dossier gate for committing a new scene.\nAsk: Is this model developed enough to explain the consequential choices and outcomes in the planned story? Identify the important explanatory dependencies, then inspect them where relevant: whole-life trends and flaws that affect choices; concepts and what their distinctions mean; physical quantities, capacities and bottlenecks; institutions, incentives and constraints; causal Events, alternatives, anticipation and adaptation; author processes for intentional withholding and later resolution. Choose subjects from this story. These are prompts for attention, not a mandatory taxonomy, fixed list of life processes, decomposition quota, or demand for a shock in every scene.\nInclude the processes underlying consequential character speech and behavior. Inspect actual model and graph evidence for how relevant experience, learned habits, motives, attention, understanding and expectations produce a choice of words, silence or action in the present relationship and situation. Where emotions, status, anticipation, surprise or adaptation change that response, inspect the causal connection and its limits. A voice adjective, catchphrase or assertion that two characters differ does not explain their conduct. Numerical tendencies need defined meanings and links to the modeled response; a score alone cannot establish it. Do not require a universal voice taxonomy or forced differences: shared language, restraint and situation-dependent variation can be well explained. Keep authorial selection, narrator presentation and the character's own processes distinct, with each speaker's knowledge bounded by the story. When reviewing an existing draft, use its passages to identify the consequential speech and actions requiring explanation; literary recognizability and effectiveness still require a separate actual-prose review and are advisory.\nFor each reviewed subject, give a concise sufficient, needs_opening, or unclear finding with evidence from actual model records and selected graph nodes. Where the work claims a consequential causal connection, inspect how the relevant circumstances and history bear on what the person knows, wants or can do and on the action and its consequences. Explore plausible alternatives when they reveal a useful distinction; this is one avenue of inquiry, not a required scene pattern or a simulated counterfactual. Identify an unsupported claimed connection as a gap rather than repeating the intended plot. Separate the character's condition and understanding from an author's or reader's interpretation. Explain why the existing abstraction is enough for this focus, or specify a useful refinement/evidence needed. A sufficient finding is a local judgment and leaves the model open to fresh questions. A name, generic process label, numerical score or plot assertion alone is not an explanation. Numerical categories must have meaningful comparisons and units. Preserve intentionally unknown causes, competing accounts, quiet scenes, ambiguity and distinctive choices; do not manufacture certainty to pass a review. Judge whether the scene respects what is established and what remains open, not whether all mysteries have been resolved. Do not demand extra detail or a flaw on every page. Separate a necessary explanatory repair from an optional artistic preference; this is not a literary grade.\nRecord coverage and findings with life_story_model_depth_record using the exact taskHash. Cite model evidence as {kind: \"model\", ref: \"process:<id>\"} (or event:, cut:, concept:, abstract_cut:, event_relation:, referent:, binding:, realization:, law:, claim:), optionally with a JSON Pointer path inside that record, or as a full JSON Pointer path; the server resolves refs against the bound model. Findings become an Understanding Node with links to their graph and model evidence. Save gaps honestly rather than marking them sufficient to pass. Repair only the relevant model parts through existing tools, preserve unaffected character/history, then repeat the depth review on the changed basis and re-review affected prose. A new or consequentially changed story plan must be stored and reviewed; do not continue from an external plan. Reuse a sufficient review only while its focus, source, dossier and relevant context remain unchanged and cover the intended scene. Incidental draft or note additions do not require repeating it.\nWhen rebinding a narrative graph to a successor model, use life_narrative_revise to retain earlier depth-assessment nodes as historical records but remove their predecessor-model anchor edges from that successor only. Native model anchors must resolve against the graph's current source. Never retarget an old finding's path to new model values. The immutable predecessor graph and each assessment's reviewedGraphHash/modelHash preserve its exact evidence. Then record a fresh assessment with new anchors; historical assessments cannot authorize scenes against the changed source. Review other affected anchors explicitly under the existing graph revision contract.\nThe calling LLM supplies the judgment. The server verifies references, recorded coverage, source identity and freshness, not explanatory truth, completeness, hidden reasoning, or literary merit. Use an independent reviewer when available; otherwise identify self-review. Model-definition reads are administrative and not scope-filtered. They describe static structure and initial values, not current values in a frozen world/candidate snapshot; inspect appropriate bound evidence for runtime claims and mark unavailable evidence unclear.\n\nDevelop or reuse a model of the author's voice during exploration and before preparing new scenes for commitment, within the agreed brief and human involvement, derived from the author's life in its own life model (life_story_world_record, stage author_reader). Exploratory drafts can reveal new aspects of that voice and life; follow those questions back into the model without requiring a settled account before trying a passage. Store it with life_story_author_record, kind author_model, using data with schema meaning-model-story-author-model/v1. Its modeledAuthorId is the person/persona being modeled; the tool's authorId identifies the recorder. Keep the model author-only and separate from story-world character life trends. For an existing project, reuse its chosen model; an explicit request to omit author modeling or a bounded review/edit remains valid. Do not silently invent a model of the real user in an autonomous story run: create a clearly fictional author persona when authorial choices have been delegated and no real author model was supplied, recording that choice.\nModel causes of style: supplied preferences or relevant experience, observations from actual writing samples, tentative interpretations, or invented persona history lead to outlook and habitual attention, which lead to concrete writing choices. In real_author mode use supplied material and distinguish interpretation from what the author actually said; a narrator's statements are not evidence of the author's biography or beliefs. Do not fabricate private experiences. Fictional author material must be labeled invented. The life itself belongs in the author's life model; this record holds the voice that life produces. Numerical dimensions can describe chosen comparisons and tendencies with explicit meanings, units, bounds and values; they are authored models, not universal personality scores. Existing numerical life exploration can inform a fictional author's development when useful; keep its samples and conclusions in the graph.\nFor new writing, explicitly locate the author at the time of composition: their life stage and current circumstances, relevant earlier life and writing history (including influences, experiments and habits changed or retained), and their reasons for writing this particular work now. Store supported or invented context as labeled basis entries and link its relevant effects through dispositions; no new record type is needed. Only experience available at that composition point may shape this version of the author. Use known real-author information; leave unavailable life history or motives explicitly unknown in the record summary, without inventing evidence or demanding private biography. For a delegated fictional persona, choose and record these elements as invented. Reasons can be multiple, conflicting, uncertain or evolving: curiosity, pleasure, craft, a commission, earning a living, remembrance or questioning a conviction are all possible. An exploratory work need not have a settled thesis. Keep reasons for undertaking the work separate from a chapter's purpose, narrator or character motives, and the effect actually achieved for a reader. The connections may shape subject, form, voice, emphasis or omission without requiring autobiographical exposition or a message in every scene. Revisit them when useful during review; preserve the earlier record and explicitly revise changed motives rather than retrofitting an intention to declare the draft successful.\nThe data object requires schema, modeledAuthorId, mode (real_author or fictional_author), label, basis and dispositions; dimensions is optional. Each basis entry has id, kind (author_statement, writing_sample, interpretation or invented), description, and optional sourceNodeId/excerpt. Writing samples require a stored source node and exact excerpt. Each disposition has id, names basisIds and explains outlookOrHabit, writingConsequences (an array), usefulContexts, risksOrCounterweights and optional dimensionIds. Optional dimensions have id, meaning, comparisonQuestion, unit, minimum, maximum and value. For example, work negotiating between institutions may prompt attention to who can interrupt or name a problem, expressed through asymmetrical dialogue; its counterweight is allowing uncalculated affection and encounters outside institutions. Keep the experience, interpretation and proposed literary effect distinct rather than assigning stock adjectives or equating a background with one inevitable style.\nCarry the exact stored authorModelNodeId into scene preparation. In scene.authorApplication select relevant dispositionIds and describe intendedEffect, restraint and narratorRelation. Vary attention, distance, syntax, rhythm, image sources, treatment of dialogue, explanation and omission where the model gives a reason; these are examples, not required dimensions or sentence quotas. A contrasting narrator, an unusual register or deliberately leaving a disposition inactive can be appropriate. Do not force every disposition into every scene or make all characters sound like the author. The author, recorder, narrator and focal character are separate identities; author knowledge or beliefs do not grant character knowledge, narrator authority or fictional truth. No private author background should appear in prose merely because it shaped a choice.\nGround character speech and behavior in the characters' own modeled processes, not in the author model alone. Where consequential, connect what a character notices, wants, expects, understands and has learned to how they speak, withhold, act and respond to others. Consider relationship and status, emotional state, anticipation, surprise and adaptation as relevant causes rather than a required list of traits. The same person can speak differently in safety, negotiation or grief while retaining a recognizable history. Give these connections evidence in the existing model and graph; an adjective-only voice label, accent or catchphrase is not a substitute. Do not invent universal voice axes, force contrast between every pair of characters, or give a speaker knowledge unavailable to them. Shared language and deliberate resemblance can be meaningful.\nAutomatically review the actual prose after a draft and after a substantive revision. Ask explicitly: Does this work express the modeled author's voice at this point in their life, and where does the text support or undermine that reading? Are the important characters' voices and actions credible and recognizable through their own underlying processes, including meaningful changes by situation? Assess the author separately and give an individual finding for each relevant principal character. If author modeling was omitted, record that limit rather than inventing an author profile. For characters who act without speaking, examine behavior and viewpoint where available rather than inventing dialogue.\nEach finding must distinguish intended voice from observed effects, cite exact draft passages and identify the relevant author-model dispositions or character-process evidence through graph node IDs or model paths. Explain recognizability, useful distinction or similarity, and variation by situation; record weaknesses or uncertainty honestly. Give the smallest useful repair, or explain why to keep what works. Examine attention, narrative distance, rhythm, imagery, dialogue, action and omission where useful; do not replace reading with a checklist, enforced imitation or a quota for every trait. Distinguish purposeful narrator contrast or shared character language from an unintended flattening of voices. A voice is assessed against the chosen model and text, not claimed to be a real person's objectively true voice. A reader's interpretation of a narrator or character is not evidence of the real author's private beliefs or biography.\nStore the assessment inside the graph using life_story_author_record with kind assessment, producing an actual externalized_reflection Understanding Node, not metadata or an exported review alone. Link about the exact reviewed draft/passage nodes and shaped_by the selected author model when present; link relevant graph process evidence as appropriate. In data preserve the reviewed graphHash, sourceSnapshotHash and modelHash, the selected author model ID and record hash when supplied, and per-subject findings with their prose citations and model evidence node IDs or paths. Use the exact identities and hashes available in the review task or graph; retrieve missing evidence rather than fabricate it, and identify unavailable evidence as a limit. These findings externalize the evidence and conclusions needed for revision, not hidden reasoning. Save them before treating voice review as complete. Use the optional authorModelNodeId in life_story_purpose_review so its advice uses the exact graph model rather than a caller summary. Literary effectiveness remains advisory, not a style score or hard gate.\nWhen a voice is weak, distinguish a prose realization problem from an inadequately explained character process or author interpretation. A later deepening pass can strengthen an existing causal connection or its expression while preserving successful scenes and variation; more detail, difference or intensity is not automatically better. Reassess changed passages after revision and preserve earlier findings as historical evidence rather than rewriting them to match the new draft.\nRecord changed author models as new author_model records linked supersedes, then prepare and review affected prose against the chosen revision. Style-only changes need not invalidate an otherwise unchanged causal depth review; changes to story causes or disclosure do. The server validates structure, sources and provenance, not whether the model captures a person or produces distinctive writing.","responseGuidance":"Briefly identify the purpose(s) and whether each is author-stated or inferred; give a qualitative judgment (fulfilled, partly_fulfilled, not_fulfilled, or unclear) with textual evidence. Consider character and reader anticipation, change, and adaptation where relevant. Include individual evidenced author/character voice findings under the voice-review instructions and save them as Understanding Nodes. Add at most one revision suggestion, only if useful, as the overall editorial recommendation; voice findings may identify subject-specific repairs or reasons to keep the prose. Identify whether a suggestion repairs coherence or offers an artistic alternative and what passage or model assumption it affects.","evaluator":"calling_llm","assessment":null,"advisoryOnly":true,"contextCompletenessVerified":false,"worldMutation":false,"graphMutation":false,"taskHash":"496def37451232dc600736a7bdc9ff901b88e40d562722c49f7df4544119535b"},"currentSignatureUpdate":{"previousModelHash":"028552f2c3f584c4e6cb9b526b73cff5618399df19860cd732b4c700e451ad67","currentModelHash":"a4f657396560ee12f1aff27c835aa3aab891192b61962413d48a02a4eb48e248","changed":"Only six Cut provenance lists: original entries retained; fresh reviewer attribution, scope and current carrier signatures appended.","scope":"The four carriers are in the authored inner-life context, not lens/understanding reading Events, so the public reading-evidence function resolves these signatures to the carriers. A later supporting E20 change must trigger the linked UnderstandingNode review, not be falsely represented as a changed numeric text signature."}}}
nodes.title: Six succession readings reviewed; four carriers repaired

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"decision","text":"Use located_in for physical Event settings and coordinate/position bindings for position-process subjects. Different roles retain their meaning. Local scene frames are independently authored fictional tableaux, without a geographic transform. The date intervals locate representative configurations within coarse scene envelopes; they do not assert day- or month-long immobility. No speed, route interpolation, continuous motion or numeric uncertainty is inferred. These snapshots enrich the spatial model without certifying physical completeness."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"plan","text":"Develop the existing native knowledge/work processes from the accepted prose and Events, preserving the whole life and the venture’s known service-capacity failure. The book already shows supervised source uncertainty, later self-comparison in an overloaded office, silence before the employer, reciprocal corrective reading, and a request for the full account in a reference. Add bounded native subevents and explicit contextual relations where those actions remain buried in aggregate Events. Preserve context-dependent recurrence: the 1852 lesson neither guarantees later interruption nor creates an independent checker. Considered an authored competence score; a single increasing scale would conflate source independence, audible intervention, employment authority and technical qualification, so qualitative distinctions are more useful for this question. No new incident, numerical allocation, chronological outcome or completed personality transformation is needed. The model can distinguish an observed action from the modeler’s explanation of it. Nora’s material attention and unsettled_account are already carried by the strip, pencil, ruler and fresh sheet; preserve their scene-specific use instead of adding an explanatory moral. Leave unobserved origins, gaps between scenes and later mastery open. Parent process origins remain unknown; a history of later responses must not be loaded into Wills’s knowledge at birth."}
nodes.title: Wills: learning to interrupt without becoming an independent checker

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"interpretation","text":"A modeler’s reading of the unchanged passages, not an extra thought silently assigned to Wills. In January 1852 “I cannot read that one” is followed by Neale’s “Nor can I”: source uncertainty becomes a permitted question. In April 1854 a second person is unavailable and self-reading fails to provide independent evidence; this does not erase the lesson. In the May inquiry “The clerk said nothing” leaves the reason for silence unsettled. In reciprocal correction “The one before, Mr Neale” succeeds only after a soft request fails, a pencil stops the copy, and Neale returns to the figure. Before departure “Only the other part as well” asks an employer to preserve his own authorization alongside Wills’s error. These are different relationships to a question and its audience, not one steadily growing quantity. The new personal subevents make those distinctions inspectable beneath the existing work/knowledge whole."}
nodes.title: What changes when Wills can stop the work?

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"revision","text":"The revision check flags the preceding development plan because the knowledge/work Event descriptions it discusses were expanded. Reviewed: the plan is retained as a historical statement of intended work, and this note records its completion. Four native personal subevents now open the accepted lesson, self-comparison, inquiry and reciprocal correction; the existing reference request stays in place. Four explicit renders declarations were added after proposal review, with every previous declaration retained. The prose, reading order, scene disclosure claims and three telling-process tracks remain unchanged; their quoted passages still support the current readings. The fresh model-depth assessment covers this changed model. Do not infer a continuous numerical trajectory, independent checker qualification or complete learning history from this repair. No other parent-world values, numerical Cuts, scene outcomes or coordinates were changed. No additional prose was needed: Nora’s material attention is already enacted in the source passages."}
nodes.title: Development plan reviewed against the accepted refinement

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"question","text":"The existing episodes support several possible openings. Does Wills’s silence before Halden arise mainly from dependence on a future reference, shame about his own error, fear of naming the authorizer, or another reading of that encounter? The manuscript does not settle it. Which part of reciprocal checking transfers to a new workplace when Neale is absent: source separation, a stopping gesture, confidence that a request will be answered, or none reliably? Does requesting a fuller employment reference alter later conduct, or remain a local success? These are possible next investigations, not missing quotas or authorization to invent the answer now. Obtaining the original specimen and later independent qualification also remain unknown. A useful subsequent scene could test one relationship rather than declare a cured personality."}
nodes.title: Where can Wills interrupt, and what makes a question safe enough to ask?
